# DeepLinkNow: full documentation

> Deep links and deferred deep links for iOS, Android, React Native and Flutter, without the attribution and ad tracking of Branch or AppsFlyer. Any path on your domain works as a link.

- DeepLinkNow does deep linking only: no attribution, no ad tracking, no advertising IDs, no ATT prompt, no cross-app data.
- Any path and query on an app's link domain (yourapp.deeplinknow.com, or a custom domain on paid plans) is a working deep link. Nothing has to be created in a dashboard first.
- After an install, the SDK's checkDeferredDeepLink() returns the path and query the user originally tapped.
- iOS: the link page copies the link to the clipboard before the App Store; the SDK reads it on first launch (iOS shows an Allow Paste prompt). A scored fingerprint match is the backup.
- Android: the click ID goes through the Google Play Install Referrer, which is exact for Play Store installs. A scored fingerprint match is the backup.
- Fingerprint matches come with confidence_score (0-100) and match_quality (HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW). An IP match is not required. The developer picks the threshold.
- Retention: A deferred link can be claimed for 1 hour after the click, and stored fingerprints are deleted within 30 days.
- SDKs: iOS (Swift, SPM and CocoaPods), Android (Kotlin, Maven Central com.deeplinknow:dln-android), React Native and Expo (npm @deeplinknow/react-native, with an Expo Router helper), Flutter (pub.dev deeplinknow, also in FlutterFlow). All on version 1.3; React Native and Flutter wrap the native SDKs.
- MCP server for coding agents (npm @deeplinknow/mcp): Claude Code, Cursor, Claude Desktop, VS Code and Windsurf can read these docs, check a link domain and plan a migration. It uses a private key only for its optional link tools.
- Apple App Site Association and assetlinks.json are generated and hosted for every app.
- Link pages load no analytics or tracking scripts, and no DeepLinkNow domain is on the AdGuard or EasyPrivacy block lists.

---
Source: https://deeplinknow.com/docs/quickstart

# Quick start guide

Get deferred deep linking working in a few minutes: one call to initialize, one call to get the deferred link.

## Prerequisites

1. A DeepLinkNow account and an app created in the dashboard. Your app gets the link domain `<alias>.deeplinknow.com`.
2. Your app's **public** API key (`dln_pub_…`) from the dashboard's **API Keys** page. Creating an app issues one public key (for the SDKs) and one private key (for your server only). The public key is always shown on the API Keys page. The private key is shown once; if you lose it, regenerate it there.
3. Your iOS **Team ID** and **Bundle ID**, and your Android **package name** and **SHA-256 certificate fingerprints**, entered in the app's settings so DeepLinkNow can serve the `.well-known` files.

Any path on your link domain works as a deep link with no setup: `https://<alias>.deeplinknow.com/products/123?ref=newsletter` delivers `/products/123` with `ref=newsletter` to your app.

To try an SDK before creating an app, use the demo key `test_api_key`. It returns mock responses.

## Choose your platform

- [React Native / Expo](#react-native)
- [iOS (Swift)](#ios-swift)
- [Android (Kotlin)](#android-kotlin)
- [Flutter](#flutter)

Building with a coding agent? Use DeepLinkNow from Claude Code, Cursor or VS Code: [install the MCP server](/docs/mcp) in one click or one command (no key needed), then ask the agent to add DeepLinkNow. It reads these docs and checks your link domain.

## React Native

```bash
npx expo install @deeplinknow/react-native   # Expo (development build)
npm install @deeplinknow/react-native && cd ios && pod install   # bare React Native
```

With Expo, add the config plugin with your link domains (`["@deeplinknow/react-native", { "domains": ["<alias>.deeplinknow.com"] }]`), which sets up Associated Domains and the Android intent filter. In bare React Native, add `applinks:<alias>.deeplinknow.com` and an `autoVerify` https intent filter by hand (see the [React Native docs](/docs/react-native)). Then:

```typescript
import DeepLinkNow from "@deeplinknow/react-native";

await DeepLinkNow.initialize("dln_pub_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx");

const link = await DeepLinkNow.checkDeferredDeepLink();
if (link) {
  // link.source: "clipboard" (iOS), "referrer" (Android) or "fingerprint"
  router.push({ pathname: link.path, params: link.queryParams });
}
```

Using Expo Router? Resolve the link in `app/+native-intent.tsx` with `@deeplinknow/react-native/expo-router` instead, so the app opens straight on the right screen. See [Expo Router](/docs/react-native#expo-router).

Next: [Full React Native documentation](/docs/react-native)

## iOS (Swift)

```ruby
pod 'DeepLinkNow', '~> 1.3'
```

Or add `https://github.com/deeplinknow/dln-ios` with Swift Package Manager. Add `applinks:<alias>.deeplinknow.com` under **Signing & Capabilities → Associated Domains**. Then:

```swift
import DeepLinkNow

await DeepLinkNow.initialize(config: DLNConfig(apiKey: "dln_pub_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"))

if let link = await DeepLinkNow.checkDeferredDeepLink() {
    // Pasteboard first (exact), then fingerprint (scored)
    router.open(path: link.path, query: link.queryParams)
}
```

Handle Universal Links when the app is already installed:

```swift
.onOpenURL { url in
    if let link = DeepLinkNow.parseLink(url) {
        router.open(path: link.path, query: link.queryParams)
    }
}
```

Next: [Full iOS documentation](/docs/ios)

## Android (Kotlin)

```kotlin
dependencies {
    implementation("com.deeplinknow:dln-android:1.3.0")
}
```

Add an `autoVerify` https intent filter for `<alias>.deeplinknow.com` to your link-handling activity. Then:

```kotlin
// Application.onCreate
DLN.init(context = this, apiKey = "dln_pub_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx")

// First activity
lifecycleScope.launch {
    DLN.checkDeferredDeepLink().getOrNull()?.let { link ->
        // Install Referrer first (exact), then fingerprint (scored)
        router.open(link.path, link.queryParams)
    }
}
```

Next: [Full Android documentation](/docs/android)

## Flutter

```bash
flutter pub add deeplinknow
```

The plugin wraps the native iOS and Android SDKs, which Swift Package Manager or CocoaPods and Gradle fetch for you. Add the Associated Domains entitlement and the `autoVerify` intent filter as for the native SDKs. Then:

```dart
import 'package:deeplinknow/deeplinknow.dart';

await DeepLinkNow.initialize('dln_pub_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx');

final link = await DeepLinkNow.checkDeferredDeepLink();
if (link != null) {
  // link.source: clipboard (iOS), referrer (Android) or fingerprint
  router.go(link.fullPath);
}
```

Next: [Full Flutter documentation](/docs/flutter)

## How the deferred link is found

| | iOS | Android |
|---|---|---|
| Step 1 (exact) | Pasteboard: the landing page copied the tapped link | Play Install Referrer: the landing page passed a click ID to the Play Store |
| Step 2 (best effort) | Fingerprint match | Fingerprint match |
| Result | `DeferredDeepLink` with `source`, `confidenceScore`, `matchQuality` | same |

Every SDK returns the same `DeferredDeepLink` shape: `path`, `queryParams`, `fullPath`, `url`, `source`, `confidenceScore` (0–100) and `matchQuality` (`HIGH` / `MEDIUM` / `LOW`). Exact sources report `100` / `HIGH`.

### About fingerprint matching

- The server compares the device with clicks on your link pages from the last 1 hour and returns scored candidates. Each has a `confidence_score` (0–100) and a `match_quality`: `HIGH` (75+), `MEDIUM` (50–74), `LOW` (30–49).
- An IP match is not required, because iCloud Private Relay and carrier NAT often give the app a different IP from the browser.
- The time score decays across the 1-hour claim window, and missing data never counts as a match.
- You choose the threshold. The optional `minConfidence` filter is off by default, so you get the server's best candidate and decide what to do with its `matchQuality`.

## Troubleshooting

### Links open the browser instead of the app

- Check the dashboard settings (Team ID + Bundle ID, package name + SHA-256 fingerprints).
- Open `https://<alias>.deeplinknow.com/.well-known/apple-app-site-association` and `/.well-known/assetlinks.json`. Changes can take up to 5 minutes to appear.
- iOS caches the association file when the app is installed. Reinstall after changing it.
- Android: run `adb shell pm get-app-links <your.package>`.

### No deferred link on first launch

- Make sure you call `checkDeferredDeepLink()` after `initialize`, and that the install happened within 1 hour of the click for fingerprint matching.
- It returns a link only once per install. Call `resetDeferredDeepLink()` (or pass `force: true`) to test again.
- Turn on `enableLogs` to see each step's outcome.
- On iOS, tapping **Don't Allow** on the paste prompt skips the pasteboard step; fingerprint matching still runs.

## Need help?

- Email: support@deeplinknow.com
- [Integration checklist](/docs/integration-checklist)

---
Source: https://deeplinknow.com/docs/ios

# DeepLinkNow iOS SDK

## Overview

When a user taps one of your links before installing your app, the DeepLinkNow iOS SDK (`DeepLinkNow`, Swift) hands your app the path and query they tapped on first launch. It is not an analytics or attribution SDK. It never reads the advertising identifier (IDFA), never triggers the App Tracking Transparency prompt, and needs no ATT consent.

On iOS the deferred link comes from two sources, tried in this order:

1. **Pasteboard (exact).** The landing page copies the tapped link before sending the user to the App Store. On first launch the SDK reads it back.
2. **Fingerprint (best effort).** If the pasteboard has no link of yours, the SDK asks the server for scored candidates from clicks on your link pages in the last hour.

You get both with one call: `checkDeferredDeepLink()`.

## Requirements

- iOS 13.0+
- Swift 5.5+ (async/await)
- Xcode 13.2+
- No `Info.plist` keys are required. iOS has no pasteboard usage-description key.

## Installation

### Swift Package Manager

In Xcode choose **File > Add Package Dependencies...** and enter `https://github.com/deeplinknow/dln-ios`, or add it to `Package.swift`:

```swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/deeplinknow/dln-ios.git", from: "1.3.0")
```

### CocoaPods

```ruby
pod 'DeepLinkNow', '~> 1.3'
```

Then run `pod install`. If it says no spec satisfies `DeepLinkNow (~> 1.3)`, your local CocoaPods spec cache is older than the release: run `pod install --repo-update` once.

### Universal Links (Associated Domains)

1. In the dashboard, set your app's **Team ID / App ID prefix** and **Bundle ID**. DeepLinkNow serves `https://<alias>.deeplinknow.com/.well-known/apple-app-site-association` (and the same file for a verified custom domain) from those values. Changes are live within 5 minutes.
2. In Xcode, open **Signing & Capabilities → Associated Domains** and add `applinks:<alias>.deeplinknow.com`, plus `applinks:<your-custom-domain>` if you have one.
3. Pass incoming URLs to `parseLink` (see [Handling links that open the app](#handling-links-that-open-the-app)).

## Getting started

### Initialize the SDK

Use your app's **public** API key (`dln_pub_…`) from the dashboard's **API Keys** page. The SDK endpoints (`/api/v1/sdk/*`) reject private keys, and a private key must never ship inside an app.

```swift
import DeepLinkNow

let config = DLNConfig(
    apiKey: "dln_pub_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx",
    enableLogs: false           // true while developing
)
do {
    let app = try await DeepLinkNow.initializeThrowing(config: config)
    print("Link domains:", app.linkDomains)
} catch let error as DeepLinkNowError {
    // .invalidApiKey, .accountInactive, .noCredits, .rateLimited, .network, .server,
    // .invalidResponse, .invalidConfiguration
    print("DeepLinkNow init failed:", error.code)
}
```

`DLNConfig` options:

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `apiKey` | — | Your public key |
| `enableLogs` | `false` | Debug logging with the `[DeepLinkNow]` prefix. The API key is never logged. |
| `baseUrl` | `https://deeplinknow.com` | API base URL. A trailing `/` is fine. |
| `timeout` | `10` s | Per request |
| `retryAttempts` | `2` | Retries for transient failures (network, timeouts, 5xx, 429) |

`await DeepLinkNow.initialize(config:)` never throws: it logs failures instead, and you can check `DeepLinkNow.isInitialized` and `DeepLinkNow.initializationError` (or `DeepLinkNow.lastError`). Initialization never reads the pasteboard and never asks for a permission. A non-https `baseUrl` is refused (http only for localhost).

For local testing before you have created an app, you can use the demo key `test_api_key`. It returns mock responses and never touches real data.

### Get the deferred deep link

Call `checkDeferredDeepLink()` once on launch, after `initialize`:

```swift
if let link = await DeepLinkNow.checkDeferredDeepLink() {
    // link.path        "/products/123"
    // link.queryParams ["ref": .string("newsletter")]
    // link.source      .clipboard or .fingerprint
    // link.confidenceScore 0-100, link.matchQuality HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW
    router.open(path: link.path, query: link.queryParams)
}
// No link? Carry on to your normal start screen.
```

`checkDeferredDeepLink()` never throws. `nil` means there was no link, or the check failed (not initialized, offline, invalid key…). A failure is logged as a warning and kept in `DeepLinkNow.lastError` (a `DeepLinkNowError`: `.notInitialized`, `.network`, `.rateLimited`, …) until the next successful check, and it doesn't use up the first launch, so the SDK tries again on the next call. If you'd rather handle the error yourself, use the throwing variant:

```swift
do {
    if let link = try await DeepLinkNow.checkDeferredDeepLinkThrowing() {
        router.open(path: link.path, query: link.queryParams)
    }
} catch let error as DeepLinkNowError {
    print("Deferred check failed:", error.code)
}
```

How `checkDeferredDeepLink()` works:

1. **Pasteboard**: if the pasteboard holds a link on one of your link domains (`<alias>.deeplinknow.com` or your verified custom domain), it is parsed locally and returned with `source = .clipboard`, `confidenceScore = 100`, `matchQuality = .high`. No server match call is made.
2. **Fingerprint**: otherwise the SDK calls `POST /api/v1/sdk/match` and returns the best candidate the server sent, with the server's `confidence_score` and `match_quality` unchanged (`source = .fingerprint`).

It returns a link at most once per install. After a definitive answer (a link, or nothing found) later calls return `nil` without touching the pasteboard or the network. Errors don't count, so an offline first launch can still succeed on the next launch.

Options (`DLNDeferredOptions`):

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `minConfidence` | `nil` (off) | Discard fingerprint candidates whose `confidence_score` is below this value. Pasteboard results are exact and are never filtered. |
| `useClipboard` | `true` | Read the pasteboard first. Set `false` to skip it and rely on fingerprinting only. |
| `force` | `false` | Ignore the "already checked" flag (useful while testing). |

```swift
let link = await DeepLinkNow.checkDeferredDeepLink(
    DLNDeferredOptions(minConfidence: 50, useClipboard: true)
)
```

`DeepLinkNow.resetDeferredDeepLink()` clears the first-launch flag so you can test the flow again without reinstalling.

### The result: `DLNDeferredDeepLink`

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `path` | The tapped path up to the first `?`, not decoded, always starting with `/` |
| `queryParams` | Query parameters with `URLSearchParams` semantics: a string, a flag (`?k`), or a list for repeated keys |
| `fullPath` | Path and query exactly as tapped |
| `url` | Absolute https URL of the link |
| `source` | `.clipboard` or `.fingerprint` (`.referrer` exists for parity with Android) |
| `confidenceScore` | `0`–`100`. Server score for fingerprint results, `100` for the pasteboard |
| `matchQuality` | `HIGH` (75+), `MEDIUM` (50–74) or `LOW` (30–49) |
| `deeplinkId`, `targetUrl`, `campaignId`, `metadata`, `matchedAt`, `expiresAt` | From the server (fingerprint results) |
| `matchDetails` | Score breakdown (fingerprint results) |

## How fingerprint matching works

Fingerprint matching is the backup for when the pasteboard is empty, the user denied the paste prompt, or you set `useClipboard: false`.

- The landing page stores a small description of the click: IP address, device class, OS version, screen size, language, time zone, and the path and query that were tapped.
- On first launch the SDK sends the same kind of description of the device. The server compares it with clicks on **your** app's link pages from the **last 1 hour** and returns up to 10 candidates, best first.
- Each candidate has a `confidence_score` (0–100) and a `match_quality`: `HIGH` (75+), `MEDIUM` (50–74) or `LOW` (30–49). Candidates below 30 are not returned.
- **An IP match is not required.** iCloud Private Relay and carrier NAT often give the app a different IP from Safari, so the server also considers clicks from the same device class with a matching screen or OS version.
- Score weights: IP 40, device 27 (screen 15, OS version 12), time 18, locale 15 (time zone 10, language 5). Device points count only when the platform and device class agree (an iPad click never scores for an iPhone). When the browser couldn't report its real iOS version (Chrome for iOS, in-app browsers such as Instagram's), a compatible OS version earns 6 instead of 12. Missing data never counts as agreement.
- The time score decays linearly across the 1-hour claim window: full marks within 5 minutes, half at about 32 minutes, zero at 60 minutes.
- So without an IP match, a match where everything else agrees scores 60 (MEDIUM), or 54 from Chrome for iOS or an in-app browser. Each match in the `/sdk/match` response carries `score_version` (`2` since October 2026). If you tuned `minConfidence` on the old weights (IP 40, device 30, time 20, locale 10), check it again: Chrome for iOS and in-app browser matches without an IP match moved from 60 to 54.
- **You choose the threshold.** `checkDeferredDeepLink()` returns the server's best candidate as is. The `minConfidence` filter is off by default. Use `matchQuality` or `confidenceScore` to decide, for example, to route `HIGH` matches straight away and confirm `MEDIUM` or `LOW` ones with the user.

Once a device gets a `MEDIUM` or better match, the click is claimed for that device, so another phone on the same Wi-Fi doesn't receive it too.

## The pasteboard and the paste prompt

On iOS 16+, reading a link that Safari copied shows the system prompt **"App would like to paste from Safari"**. The SDK keeps this to a minimum:

- It reads the pasteboard only during `checkDeferredDeepLink()` on first launch (or when you call `checkClipboard()` yourself), never at init and never in the background.
- On iOS 14+ it first checks for a web URL with `detectPatterns`, which shows no prompt. If there is no URL, it skips straight to fingerprinting.
- If the user taps **Don't Allow**, that counts as "nothing found" and the SDK continues with fingerprinting.
- It never writes to or clears the pasteboard, and never logs content that is not one of your links.

If you don't want the prompt, pass `useClipboard: false`, or show your own "Paste your link" button with `UIPasteControl` (iOS 16+) and pass the result to `parseLink`.

## Handling links that open the app

When the app is already installed, a Universal Link opens it directly. Parse it with `parseLink`, which returns `nil` for URLs that are not on your link domains:

```swift
// SwiftUI
.onOpenURL { url in
    if let link = DeepLinkNow.parseLink(url) {
        router.open(path: link.path, query: link.queryParams)
    }
}

// UIKit (SceneDelegate)
func scene(_ scene: UIScene, continue userActivity: NSUserActivity) {
    guard userActivity.activityType == NSUserActivityTypeBrowsingWeb,
          let url = userActivity.webpageURL,
          let link = DeepLinkNow.parseLink(url) else { return }
    router.open(path: link.path, query: link.queryParams)
}
```

Deferred results and direct opens use the same parsing rules, so you can route both the same way.

## Low-level API

The building blocks behind `checkDeferredDeepLink()` stay available:

| Method | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `findDeferredUserThrowing()` / `findDeferredUser()` | Every fingerprint candidate from `/api/v1/sdk/match`, unfiltered: `confidence_score`, `match_quality`, `match_details` and `deeplink` (with `full_path` and `query_params`), plus `ttl_seconds`. `findDeferredUser()` returns `nil` on any error; `findDeferredUserThrowing()` throws a `DeepLinkNowError` |
| `checkClipboard()` | The pasteboard text if it is exactly one URL on your link domains, else `nil` (may show the paste prompt) |
| `hasDeepLinkToken()` / `hasDeepLinkTokenAsync()` | Cheap "is there probably a URL on the pasteboard" check that never reads the content and shows no prompt |
| `parseLink(_:)` | Validate and parse a URL on your link domains into `DLNParsedLink` (`path`, `queryParams`, `fullPath`, `url`) |
| `parseDeepLink(_:)` | Older tuple form `(path, parameters)` of `parseLink(_:)` |
| `isValidDomain(_:)` | The host rule: exactly `<alias>.deeplinknow.com` or a verified custom domain, case-insensitive |
| `createDeepLink(path:customParameters:)` | Build an https link on your primary link domain that `parseLink` round-trips (`nil` before init) |
| `isInitialized`, `initializationError`, `appInfo`, `sdkVersion` | Init state and SDK version (`"1.3.0"`) |

If you call these yourself, check the pasteboard before fingerprinting:

```swift
if let copied = DeepLinkNow.checkClipboard(),
   let url = URL(string: copied),
   let link = DeepLinkNow.parseLink(url) {
    router.open(path: link.path, query: link.queryParams)
} else if let response = try? await DeepLinkNow.findDeferredUserThrowing(),
          let best = response.matches.first(where: { $0.deeplink != nil }) {
    // best.confidenceScore and best.matchQuality: your call
}
```

## Privacy

The SDK sends only what matching needs: a synthesized user agent, platform, OS version, device class (`iPhone`/`iPad`), screen size in points with scale, language, time zone, and the app-scoped vendor ID (IDFV), which the server uses only to claim a click for this install. `advertising_id` is always `null`. The server reads the IP from the connection. The SDK stores nothing on the device except the first-launch flag, and ships a privacy manifest (`PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`) with tracking set to false.

## API endpoints used

| Endpoint | Key | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/v1/sdk/init` | public | `initialize`: validates the key and account, returns your link domains |
| `POST /api/v1/sdk/match` | public | `checkDeferredDeepLink` (fingerprint step), `findDeferredUser` |

Both calls are exempt from per-minute rate limits; `init` counts toward monthly active users.

## Support

- Email: support@deeplinknow.com
- Source and issues: [github.com/deeplinknow/dln-ios](https://github.com/deeplinknow/dln-ios)

Source: https://deeplinknow.com/docs/android

# DeepLinkNow Android SDK

## Overview

When a user taps one of your links before installing your app, the DeepLinkNow Android SDK (`com.deeplinknow:dln-android`, Kotlin, class `com.deeplinknow.DLN`) hands your app the path and query they tapped on first launch. It is not an analytics or attribution SDK. It never reads the Google Advertising ID (GAID) and needs no ad-related permissions.

On Android the deferred link comes from two sources, tried in this order:

1. **Play Install Referrer (exact).** The landing page adds a click ID to the Play Store link. After install, the SDK reads it from the Install Referrer API and looks up the exact click.
2. **Fingerprint (best effort).** If there is no usable referrer, the SDK asks the server for scored candidates from clicks on your link pages in the last hour.

You get both with one call: `DLN.checkDeferredDeepLink()`. The Android SDK does not read the clipboard by default.

## Requirements

- Android API level 24+
- Kotlin 1.9+, AndroidX
- `android.permission.INTERNET` (declared by the library)

## Installation

```kotlin
// build.gradle.kts
dependencies {
    implementation("com.deeplinknow:dln-android:1.3.0")
}
```

```gradle
// build.gradle
dependencies {
    implementation 'com.deeplinknow:dln-android:1.3.0'
}
```

The library declares `android.permission.INTERNET` itself and ships consumer R8/ProGuard rules for its model classes. The Install Referrer library adds its own permission.

### App Links

1. In the dashboard, set your **package name** and your **SHA-256 signing certificate fingerprints** (debug, upload and Play App Signing). DeepLinkNow serves `https://<alias>.deeplinknow.com/.well-known/assetlinks.json` (and the same file for a verified custom domain). Changes are live within 5 minutes.
2. Add an intent filter to the activity that handles links:

```xml
<intent-filter android:autoVerify="true">
    <action android:name="android.intent.action.VIEW" />
    <category android:name="android.intent.category.DEFAULT" />
    <category android:name="android.intent.category.BROWSABLE" />
    <data android:scheme="https" android:host="myapp.deeplinknow.com" />
    <!-- add <data android:host="go.myapp.com" /> for a custom domain -->
</intent-filter>
```

3. Verify with `adb shell pm get-app-links <your.package>`.

## Getting started

### Initialize the SDK

Use your app's **public** API key (`dln_pub_…`) from the dashboard's **API Keys** page. The SDK endpoints (`/api/v1/sdk/*`) reject private keys, and a private key must never ship inside an app.

```kotlin
import com.deeplinknow.DLN

class MyApplication : Application() {
    override fun onCreate() {
        super.onCreate()
        // Returns immediately. Init and the Install Referrer read run in the background.
        DLN.init(this, "dln_pub_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx", enableLogs = BuildConfig.DEBUG) { result ->
            // Optional, called once on the main thread with Result<DLNAppInfo>
            result.onFailure { Log.w("App", "DeepLinkNow init failed: ${it.message}") }
        }
    }
}
```

`DLN.init` returns immediately and never blocks the main thread. It validates the key, loads your link domains and starts reading the Install Referrer in the background. Observe the outcome with `onComplete`, `DLN.awaitInitialization()` or `DLN.isInitialized`.

Optional parameters: `baseUrl` (default `https://deeplinknow.com`), `timeoutMs` (default 10 000), `retryAttempts` (default 2), and `overrideScreenWidth` / `overrideScreenHeight` / `overridePixelRatio` for reproducible matching on emulators.

For local testing before you have created an app, you can use the demo key `test_api_key`. It returns mock responses and never touches real data.

### Get the deferred deep link

Call `checkDeferredDeepLink()` once on launch, after `DLN.init`. It never throws: it returns a Kotlin `Result`.

```kotlin
lifecycleScope.launch {
    DLN.checkDeferredDeepLink()
        .onSuccess { link ->
            if (link != null) {
                // link.path        "/products/123"
                // link.queryParams {"ref": QueryValue.Single("newsletter")}
                // link.source      REFERRER or FINGERPRINT
                // link.confidenceScore 0-100, link.matchQuality HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW
                router.open(link.path, link.queryParams)
            }
        }
        .onFailure { e ->
            val error = e as DLNException // error.code: NOT_INITIALIZED, NETWORK, RATE_LIMITED, ...
            // Errors are not "no link": the SDK tries again on the next call.
        }
}
```

`checkDeferredDeepLink` is a static method on `DLN`. From Java, use the callback overload:

```java
DLN.checkDeferredDeepLink(null, false, new DeferredDeepLinkCallback() {
    @Override public void onResult(DeferredDeepLink link, DLNException error) { /* main thread */ }
});
```

How `checkDeferredDeepLink()` works:

1. **Install Referrer**: the SDK waits for the referrer, extracts the `fp_id` (or `deeplink_id`) the landing page added, and calls `GET /api/v1/sdk/referrer-lookup`. A hit is returned with `source = REFERRER`, `confidenceScore = 100`, `matchQuality = HIGH`.
2. **Fingerprint**: otherwise it calls `POST /api/v1/sdk/match` and returns the best candidate the server sent, with the server's `confidence_score` and `match_quality` unchanged (`source = FINGERPRINT`).

It returns a link at most once per install. After a definitive answer (a link, or nothing found) later calls return `null` without network access. Errors such as being offline don't count, so the next launch tries again. The Play Store keeps the referrer for 90 days.

Parameters:

| Parameter | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `minConfidence` | `null` (off) | Discard fingerprint candidates whose `confidence_score` is below this value. Referrer results are exact and never filtered. |
| `force` | `false` | Ignore the "already checked" flag (useful while testing). |

`DLN.resetDeferredDeepLink()` clears the first-launch flag and the cached referrer result so you can test the flow again without reinstalling.

### The result: `DeferredDeepLink`

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `path` | The tapped path up to the first `?`, not decoded, always starting with `/` |
| `queryParams` | `Map<String, QueryValue>` with `URLSearchParams` semantics: `Single(value)`, `Flag` (`?k` or `?k=`), `Multiple(values)` (repeated key). `toPlain()` gives `String`, `true` or `List<String>` |
| `fullPath` | Path and query exactly as tapped |
| `url` | Absolute https URL of the link |
| `source` | `DeferredDeepLinkSource.REFERRER` or `FINGERPRINT` (`.value` gives `"referrer"` / `"fingerprint"`) |
| `confidenceScore` | `0`–`100`. Server score for fingerprint results, `100` for the referrer |
| `matchQuality` | `MatchQuality.HIGH` (75+), `MEDIUM` (50–74) or `LOW` (30–49) |
| `deeplinkId`, `targetUrl`, `campaignId`, `metadata`, `matchedAt`, `expiresAt` | From the server |
| `matchDetails` | Score breakdown (fingerprint results) |

## How fingerprint matching works

Fingerprint matching is the backup for installs without a usable referrer (for example, an install that didn't come through your link's Play Store button).

- The landing page stores a small description of the click: IP address, device class, OS version, screen size, language, time zone, and the path and query that were tapped.
- The SDK sends the same kind of description of the device. The server compares it with clicks on **your** app's link pages from the **last 1 hour** and returns up to 10 candidates, best first.
- Each candidate has a `confidence_score` (0–100) and a `match_quality`: `HIGH` (75+), `MEDIUM` (50–74) or `LOW` (30–49). Candidates below 30 are not returned.
- An IP match is not required. Clicks from the same device class with a matching screen or OS version are considered too.
- Score weights: IP 40, device 27 (screen 15, OS version 12), time 18, locale 15 (time zone 10, language 5). Device points count only when the platform and device class agree. Chrome on Android always reports "Android 10", so a compatible OS version earns 6, not 12. Missing data never counts as agreement. The time score decays linearly across the 1-hour claim window.
- Each match in the `/sdk/match` response carries `score_version` (`2` since October 2026). If you tuned `minConfidence` on the old weights (IP 40, device 30, time 20, locale 10), check it again: the same device without an IP match now scores 54 rather than 60.
- **You choose the threshold.** The `minConfidence` filter is off by default. Use `matchQuality` or `confidenceScore` to decide what to route automatically and what to confirm with the user.

## Handling links that open the app

Pass incoming URLs to `DLN.parseDeepLink(url)` in both `onCreate` and `onNewIntent`. It returns `ParsedDeepLink(path, queryParams, fullPath, url)`, or `null` for URLs that are not on your link domains:

```kotlin
override fun onNewIntent(intent: Intent) {
    super.onNewIntent(intent)
    handleIntent(intent)
}

private fun handleIntent(intent: Intent) {
    val url = intent.data?.toString() ?: return
    DLN.parseDeepLink(url)?.let { link ->
        router.open(link.path, link.queryParams)
    }
}
```

Alternatively register a callback with `DLN.setDeepLinkCallback(...)` and call `DLN.handleDeepLink(url)`.

Deferred results and direct opens use the same parsing rules, so you can route both the same way. The host rule accepts exactly `<alias>.deeplinknow.com` and your verified custom domain, case-insensitively. Other `deeplinknow.com` subdomains and lookalike hosts are rejected.

## Low-level API

| Method | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `DLN.findDeferredUserResult()` | `Result<MatchResponse>`: every fingerprint candidate from `/api/v1/sdk/match`, unfiltered, in server order, each with `confidenceScore`, `matchQuality`, `matchDetails` and `deeplink` (`queryParams`, `fullPath`) |
| `getInstance().findDeferredUser()` | 1.0 API: `MatchResponse?` (null on any error) |
| `getInstance().getDeferredDeepLink()` | 1.0 API: the cached referrer result, returned on every launch. Prefer `DLN.checkDeferredDeepLink()` |
| `getInstance().getReferrerData()` | The raw Install Referrer data (`referrerString`, `fpId`, `deeplinkId`, `processedAt`) |
| `getInstance().checkClipboard()` | The clipboard text if, trimmed, it is exactly one URL on your link domains, else `null`. On Android 12+ reading shows a system "pasted" toast |
| `getInstance().hasDeepLinkToken()` | Checks the clip description only (no toast) |
| `DLN.parseDeepLink(url)` | `ParsedDeepLink(path, queryParams, fullPath, url)` or `null` |
| `DLN.isValidDomain(host)` | The host rule |
| `getInstance().parseDeepLink(url)` | Deprecated 1.0 API returning a `Pair` (decoded path, first value of repeated keys); use `DLN.parseDeepLink(url)` |

## Privacy

The SDK sends only what matching needs: a synthesized user agent, platform, OS version, device model, screen size, language, time zone, and `ANDROID_ID` (app-scoped), which the server uses only to claim a click for this install. `advertising_id` is always `null`. The server reads the IP from the connection. On the device the SDK stores only the first-launch flag and the referrer result, excluded from backups.

## API endpoints used

| Endpoint | Key | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/v1/sdk/init` | public | `DLN.init` |
| `GET /api/v1/sdk/referrer-lookup` | public | `checkDeferredDeepLink` (referrer step) |
| `POST /api/v1/sdk/match` | public | `checkDeferredDeepLink` (fingerprint step), `findDeferredUser` |

These calls are exempt from per-minute rate limits; `init` counts toward monthly active users.

## Support

- Email: support@deeplinknow.com
- Source and issues: [github.com/deeplinknow/dln-android](https://github.com/deeplinknow/dln-android)

---
Source: https://deeplinknow.com/docs/react-native

# DeepLinkNow React Native SDK

## Overview

`@deeplinknow/react-native` gives React Native and Expo apps the same two calls as the native SDKs: initialize, and get the deferred deep link. It wraps the native iOS and Android SDKs, so it behaves the same way and returns the same shapes on both platforms.

When a user taps one of your links before installing your app, `checkDeferredDeepLink()` returns the path and query they tapped:

- **iOS**: 1. the link the landing page copied to the pasteboard (exact), then 2. fingerprint matching (best effort).
- **Android**: 1. the Play Install Referrer (exact), then 2. fingerprint matching (best effort).

It is not an analytics or attribution SDK. It never reads advertising identifiers and never triggers the App Tracking Transparency prompt.

## Requirements

- React Native 0.81+ (old or new architecture), or Expo SDK 54+ with a development build
- iOS 13+, Android API 24+
- Expo Go has no native code, so only the fingerprint step works there (the SDK logs a warning). Use a development build.

## Installation

### Expo

```sh
npx expo install @deeplinknow/react-native
```

Add the config plugin with your link domains. It adds `applinks:<domain>` to the iOS Associated Domains and an auto-verified App Links intent filter on Android for each domain:

```json
{
  "expo": {
    "plugins": [
      ["@deeplinknow/react-native", { "domains": ["myapp.deeplinknow.com", "go.myapp.com"] }]
    ]
  }
}
```

Then rebuild the native projects: `npx expo prebuild` (or let EAS Build do it), then `npx expo run:ios` / `npx expo run:android`.

### Bare React Native

```sh
npm install @deeplinknow/react-native
cd ios && pod install
```

If `pod install` (or `npx expo prebuild`) says no spec satisfies `DeepLinkNow (~> 1.3.0)`, your local CocoaPods spec cache is older than the release. Run `cd ios && pod install --repo-update` once.

Autolinking picks the right native module (TurboModule on the new architecture, bridge module on the old one). Add the Associated Domains entitlement (`applinks:myapp.deeplinknow.com`) on iOS and an `autoVerify` https intent filter for your link domains on Android. See the [iOS](/docs/ios) and [Android](/docs/android) docs for details and the dashboard settings that serve the `.well-known` files.

## Getting started

### Initialize the SDK

Use your app's **public** API key (`dln_pub_…`) from the dashboard's **API Keys** page. The SDK endpoints (`/api/v1/sdk/*`) reject private keys, and a private key must never ship inside an app.

```typescript
import DeepLinkNow from "@deeplinknow/react-native";

const app = await DeepLinkNow.initialize("dln_pub_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx", {
  enableLogs: __DEV__,
});
// app: DLNAppInfo { id, alias, domains, accountStatus, creditsRemaining }, or null if it failed
```

Config options: `enableLogs` (default `false`), `baseUrl` (default `https://deeplinknow.com`), `timeoutMs` (default 10 000), `retryAttempts` (default 2). `initialize` makes one `/init` request per call and resolves with `DLNAppInfo`. It never rejects: if it fails it resolves `null`, logs a warning and keeps the error in `DeepLinkNow.lastError`, so no `try`/`catch` is needed. `DeepLinkNow.isInitialized()` tells you whether it succeeded.

For local testing before you have created an app, you can use the demo key `test_api_key`. It returns mock responses and never touches real data.

### Get the deferred deep link

```typescript
const link = await DeepLinkNow.checkDeferredDeepLink();
if (link) {
  // link.path            "/products/123"
  // link.queryParams     { ref: "newsletter" }
  // link.source          "clipboard" | "referrer" | "fingerprint"
  // link.confidenceScore 0-100
  // link.matchQuality    "HIGH" | "MEDIUM" | "LOW"
  router.push({ pathname: link.path, params: link.queryParams });
}
```

`checkDeferredDeepLink` never throws or rejects. "No link" and a failure (offline, invalid key, not initialized) both resolve `null`, so the app just carries on to its normal start screen. To tell them apart, check `DeepLinkNow.lastError`: a `DLNError` with `code` (`notInitialized`, `network`, `rateLimited`, …), plus `status` and `serverMessage` when the server sent one. It is cleared by the next successful call.

It returns a link at most once per install. After a definitive answer (a link, or nothing found) later calls resolve to `null` without network, clipboard or referrer access. Errors don't count, so an offline first launch can still succeed on the next launch.

Options:

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `minConfidence` | unset (off) | Discard fingerprint candidates whose `confidence_score` is below this value. Clipboard and referrer results are exact and never filtered. |
| `useClipboard` | `true` | iOS only: read the pasteboard first (may show the iOS 16+ paste prompt). Ignored on Android. |
| `force` | `false` | Ignore the "already checked" flag (useful while testing). |

```typescript
const link = await DeepLinkNow.checkDeferredDeepLink({ minConfidence: 50 });
```

`await DeepLinkNow.resetDeferredDeepLink()` clears the first-launch state and the cached referrer result so you can test again without reinstalling. `clearReferrerCache()` is a deprecated alias.

Using Expo Router? See [Expo Router](#expo-router).

### The result: `DeferredDeepLink`

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | `string` | The tapped path up to the first `?`, not decoded, always starting with `/` |
| `queryParams` | `Record<string, string \| true \| string[]>` | Query parameters with `URLSearchParams` semantics; `true` for a bare flag, an array for repeated keys |
| `fullPath` | `string` | Path and query exactly as tapped |
| `url` | `string` | Absolute https URL of the link |
| `source` | `"clipboard" \| "referrer" \| "fingerprint"` | Which signal produced the answer |
| `confidenceScore` | `number` | `0`–`100`. Server score for fingerprint results, `100` for clipboard and referrer |
| `matchQuality` | `"HIGH" \| "MEDIUM" \| "LOW"` | `HIGH` 75+, `MEDIUM` 50–74, `LOW` 30–49 |
| `deeplinkId`, `targetUrl`, `campaignId`, `metadata`, `matchedAt`, `expiresAt` | optional | From the server |
| `matchDetails` | optional | Score breakdown (fingerprint results) |

## Expo Router

If your app uses Expo Router, get the deferred deep link in `app/+native-intent.tsx`. Expo Router calls this file with the URL that launched the app, before the first screen mounts. Resolving the link there means the app opens straight on the screen the user tapped: the home screen doesn't flash first, and your layouts' redirects (an auth gate, onboarding) see the right route from the start.

The minimal setup is two files. Create `app/+native-intent.tsx`:

```tsx
import { createRedirectSystemPath } from "@deeplinknow/react-native/expo-router";

export const redirectSystemPath = createRedirectSystemPath({
  apiKey: "dln_pub_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx",
});
```

And handle late links in your root layout, `app/_layout.tsx`:

```tsx
import { useDeferredDeepLink } from "@deeplinknow/react-native";
import { Stack, useRouter } from "expo-router";
import { useEffect } from "react";

export default function RootLayout() {
  const { link, clear } = useDeferredDeepLink();
  const router = useRouter();

  useEffect(() => {
    if (link) {
      clear(); // so it opens once
      router.push(link.fullPath);
    }
  }, [link]);

  return <Stack />;
}
```

**Don't skip the second file.** The helper waits at most `timeoutMs` (3 seconds by default) before the first screen mounts. If the link is found after that, for example on a slow connection, it reaches your app only through `useDeferredDeepLink()`. Without the hook, that link is dropped. The hook shares the helper's check, so the network calls run once, and a link the helper already opened comes back as `null`.

You don't need to call `DeepLinkNow.initialize` anywhere else: the helper does it.

What happens on each launch:

| The app was opened… | The helper returns |
|---|---|
| for the first time after install, from the store or the home screen | The link the user tapped before installing, e.g. `/products/123?ref=newsletter`. If there is none, or the check takes longer than `timeoutMs`, the app starts on its normal route |
| by a link on your DeepLinkNow domains (`yourapp.deeplinknow.com` or a verified custom domain) | That link's path and query, e.g. `/products/123?ref=newsletter` |
| any other way (a later launch, another URL, your own `myapp://` links) | The URL unchanged, so Expo Router handles it as usual |

The helper never throws. If something fails (offline, a wrong API key), the app starts where it would have without DeepLinkNow, and `DeepLinkNow.lastError` says why.

### Options

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `apiKey` | required | Your public API key (`dln_pub_…`) |
| `config` | `{}` | Passed to `initialize`: `enableLogs`, `baseUrl`, `timeoutMs`, `retryAttempts` |
| `minConfidence` | off | Ignore fingerprint matches scoring below this (0–100). See [How fingerprint matching works](#how-fingerprint-matching-works) |
| `useClipboard` | `true` | iOS: check the link the landing page copied first |
| `timeoutMs` | `3000` | The longest the first launch waits for the link, in milliseconds. `0` never waits |
| `mapUniversalLinks` | `true` | Rewrite links on your DeepLinkNow domains to their in-app path |
| `mapLink` | the link's `fullPath` | `(link, source) => string \| null`. Use it when your screen paths differ from your link paths. `source` is `"deferred"` or `"universal"`. Return `null` to keep the incoming URL |

For example, if your links look like `/p/123` but the screen is `app/products/[id].tsx`:

```tsx
export const redirectSystemPath = createRedirectSystemPath({
  apiKey: "dln_pub_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx",
  minConfidence: 50,
  mapLink: (link) =>
    link.path.startsWith("/p/") ? `/products/${link.path.slice(3)}` : link.fullPath,
});
```

If you already have a `redirectSystemPath` with your own rewrites, call `redirectSystemPathWithDeferredLink(event, options)` from it and apply your rewrites to the result.

### Open the link after sign-in

If a deep-linked screen needs a signed-in user, set `timeoutMs: 0` in `+native-intent.tsx` so the app starts immediately and every deferred link comes through the hook, then navigate once the user has signed in:

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx
import { useDeferredDeepLink } from "@deeplinknow/react-native";
import { Stack, useRouter } from "expo-router";
import { useEffect } from "react";

export default function RootLayout() {
  const { link, clear } = useDeferredDeepLink();
  const { isSignedIn } = useAuth(); // your auth
  const router = useRouter();

  useEffect(() => {
    if (link && isSignedIn) {
      clear(); // so it opens once
      router.push(link.fullPath);
    }
  }, [link, isSignedIn]);

  return <Stack />;
}
```

### Without Expo Router

`useDeferredDeepLink()` works in any React Native app. Pass your API key, and it initializes the SDK and checks once:

```tsx
import { useDeferredDeepLink } from "@deeplinknow/react-native";
import { useEffect } from "react";

function App() {
  const { link, isLoading, clear } = useDeferredDeepLink({ apiKey: "dln_pub_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx" });

  useEffect(() => {
    if (link) {
      clear();
      navigation.navigate("Product", { path: link.path, params: link.queryParams });
    }
  }, [link]);

  // …
}
```

It returns `{ link, isLoading, clear }`. `link` is `null` until a link is found, after `clear()`, and on every launch after the first (in Expo Go, which has no native first-launch flag, the check runs again on each launch while the click can still be claimed).

## How fingerprint matching works

- The landing page stores a small description of the click: IP address, device class, OS version, screen size, language, time zone, and the path and query that were tapped.
- The SDK sends the same kind of description of the device. The server compares it with clicks on your app's link pages from the **last 1 hour** and returns up to 10 candidates, best first, each with a `confidence_score` (0–100) and a `match_quality` (`HIGH`, `MEDIUM`, `LOW`). Candidates below 30 are not returned.
- An IP match is not required (iCloud Private Relay and carrier NAT often change the IP between browser and app).
- Missing data never counts as agreement, and the time score decays linearly across the 1-hour claim window.
- **You choose the threshold.** `minConfidence` is off by default. Use `matchQuality` or `confidenceScore` to decide what to route automatically and what to confirm with the user.

## Handling links that open the app

```typescript
import { Linking } from "react-native";

function handleUrl(url: string | null) {
  if (!url) return;
  const link = DeepLinkNow.parseDeepLink(url);
  if (link) router.push({ pathname: link.path, params: link.queryParams });
}

Linking.getInitialURL().then(handleUrl);
Linking.addEventListener("url", ({ url }) => handleUrl(url));
```

`parseDeepLink(url)` returns `{ path, queryParams, fullPath, url }`, or `null` for URLs that are not on your link domains (exactly `<alias>.deeplinknow.com` or your verified custom domain). The older `parameters` field is kept as a deprecated alias of `queryParams`.

## Low-level API

| Method | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `findDeferredUser()` | Every fingerprint candidate from `/api/v1/sdk/match` in the server's snake_case shape: `matches[]` with `confidence_score`, `match_quality`, `match_details`, `deeplink` (`target_url`, `full_path`, `query_params`, …), plus `ttl_seconds`. Resolves `null` on failure (never rejects), with the error in `DeepLinkNow.lastError` |
| `getReferrerData()` | Android only: raw Install Referrer data (`null` on iOS) |
| `checkClipboard()` | The clipboard text if it is exactly one URL on your link domains, else `null` |
| `hasDeepLinkToken()` | Cheap "is there probably a URL on the clipboard" check that shows no paste prompt |
| `parseDeepLink(url)` | Validate and parse a URL on your link domains |
| `isValidDomain(host)` | The host rule |
| `getModuleType()` | `"expo" \| "turbo" \| "bridge" \| "none"`: which native module is in use |

## Privacy

The native SDKs send only what matching needs (platform, OS version, device class, screen, language, time zone, and an app-scoped install ID used only to claim a click). `advertising_id` is always `null`. The server reads the IP from the connection.

## API endpoints used

| Endpoint | Key | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/v1/sdk/init` | public | `initialize` (exactly one call per `initialize`) |
| `GET /api/v1/sdk/referrer-lookup` | public | `checkDeferredDeepLink` on Android |
| `POST /api/v1/sdk/match` | public | `checkDeferredDeepLink` (fingerprint step), `findDeferredUser` |

## Support

- Email: support@deeplinknow.com
- Package: [npmjs.com/package/@deeplinknow/react-native](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@deeplinknow/react-native)

Source: https://deeplinknow.com/docs/flutter

# DeepLinkNow Flutter SDK

## Overview

[`deeplinknow`](https://pub.dev/packages/deeplinknow) is the Flutter plugin for DeepLinkNow. It gives Flutter and FlutterFlow apps the same two calls as the native SDKs: initialize, and get the deferred deep link.

The plugin is a thin wrapper over the native [iOS](/docs/ios) and [Android](/docs/android) SDKs (1.3). All deferred-link logic runs natively: the pasteboard and Install Referrer steps, fingerprint matching, first-launch handling and link parsing. So a Flutter app gets the same answers as a Swift, Kotlin or React Native app.

When a user taps one of your links before installing your app, `checkDeferredDeepLink()` returns the path and query they tapped:

- **iOS**: 1. the link the landing page copied to the pasteboard (exact), then 2. fingerprint matching (best effort).
- **Android**: 1. the Play Install Referrer (exact), then 2. fingerprint matching (best effort).

It is not an analytics or attribution SDK. It never reads advertising identifiers and never triggers the App Tracking Transparency prompt.

## Requirements

- Flutter 3.24+ (Dart 3.5+)
- iOS 13+, with Swift Package Manager or CocoaPods
- Android API 24+ (`minSdk 24`)
- Your app's **public** API key (`dln_pub_…`) from the dashboard's **API Keys** page

## Installation

```sh
flutter pub add deeplinknow
```

This also installs `deeplinknow_ios`, the plugin's iOS implementation. You don't add it yourself.

- **iOS**: nothing else to install. With Swift Package Manager (the default in recent Flutter) Xcode fetches `dln-ios`; with CocoaPods, `pod install` (which `flutter run` and `flutter build` run for you) fetches the `DeepLinkNow` pod. With CocoaPods, set at least `platform :ios, '13.0'` in `ios/Podfile`. No `Info.plist` keys are needed.
- **Android**: the native SDK (`com.deeplinknow:dln-android:1.3.0`) comes from Maven Central, which new Flutter projects already list in `android/settings.gradle(.kts)`. Make sure `minSdk` is at least 24 in `android/app/build.gradle(.kts)`.

Stop the app and rebuild it after adding the package. Hot restart doesn't load native code.

## Set up your link domains

DeepLinkNow serves the `.well-known` files for your domains from your dashboard settings, so links open your app when it's installed.

1. In the dashboard, set your **Team ID** and **Bundle ID** (iOS) and your **package name** and **SHA-256 certificate fingerprints** (Android).
2. **iOS**: open `ios/Runner.xcworkspace` in Xcode, go to **Runner → Signing & Capabilities → + Capability → Associated Domains**, and add `applinks:<alias>.deeplinknow.com` (and `applinks:<your custom domain>` if you have one).
3. **Android**: add an App Links intent filter to the `MainActivity` in `android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`:

```xml
<intent-filter android:autoVerify="true">
    <action android:name="android.intent.action.VIEW" />
    <category android:name="android.intent.category.DEFAULT" />
    <category android:name="android.intent.category.BROWSABLE" />
    <data android:scheme="https" android:host="<alias>.deeplinknow.com" />
</intent-filter>
```

Replace `<alias>` with your app's alias, and add one `<data>` line per custom domain.

## Getting started

### Initialize and get the deferred deep link

```dart
import 'package:deeplinknow/deeplinknow.dart';
import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart';
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

Future<void> main() async {
  WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized();

  // Never throws: null means it failed (see DeepLinkNow.lastError).
  await DeepLinkNow.initialize(
    'dln_pub_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx',
    config: const DLNConfig(enableLogs: kDebugMode),
  );

  // Delivered once per install; null on later launches.
  final link = await DeepLinkNow.checkDeferredDeepLink();

  runApp(MyApp(initialRoute: link?.path ?? '/'));
}
```

`DLNConfig` options: `enableLogs` (default `false`), `baseUrl` (default `https://deeplinknow.com`), `timeoutMs` and `retryAttempts`. Leave them unset to use the native defaults. `initialize` makes one native init per call and resolves `DLNAppInfo` (`id`, `alias`, `domains`, `primaryDomain`, …), or `null` if it failed. `DeepLinkNow.isInitialized` tells you whether the last `initialize` succeeded.

`link.path` is the path the user tapped (`/products/123`) and `link.queryParams` holds the query (`{ref: newsletter}`). Route on them the way you route any other link. With go_router:

```dart
final link = await DeepLinkNow.checkDeferredDeepLink();
if (link != null) router.go(link.fullPath); // path + query, as tapped
```

For local testing before you have created an app, you can use the demo key `test_api_key`. It returns mock responses and never touches real data.

### No link, or an error?

`checkDeferredDeepLink` never throws. "No link" and a failure (offline, invalid key, not initialized) both resolve `null`, so the app carries on to its normal start screen. To tell them apart, check `DeepLinkNow.lastError`: a `DLNError` with a `code` (`notInitialized`, `invalidApiKey`, `accountInactive`, `noCredits`, `rateLimited`, `badRequest`, `server`, `network` or `invalidResponse`, the same codes as every DeepLinkNow SDK), plus `status`, `serverMessage`, `message` and `cause` when present. It is cleared by the next successful call.

```dart
final link = await DeepLinkNow.checkDeferredDeepLink();
if (link == null && DeepLinkNow.lastError != null) {
  // Offline or misconfigured. Errors don't use up the first launch,
  // so the next launch tries again.
}
```

It returns a link at most once per install. After a definitive answer (a link, or nothing found) later calls resolve `null` without network, clipboard or referrer access.

Options:

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `minConfidence` | unset (off) | Discard fingerprint candidates whose score is below this value. Clipboard and referrer results are exact and never filtered. |
| `useClipboard` | `true` | iOS only: read the pasteboard first (may show the iOS 16+ paste prompt). Ignored on Android. |
| `force` | `false` | Ignore the "already checked" flag (useful while testing). |

```dart
final link = await DeepLinkNow.checkDeferredDeepLink(minConfidence: 50);
```

`await DeepLinkNow.resetDeferredDeepLink()` clears the first-launch state so you can test again without reinstalling. It is a test call, and it throws a `DLNError` if the native reset fails.

### The result: `DeferredDeepLink`

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | `String` | The tapped path up to the first `?`, always starting with `/` |
| `queryParams` | `Map<String, QueryValue>` | Query parameters (see below) |
| `fullPath` | `String` | Path and query exactly as tapped |
| `url` | `String` | Absolute https URL of the link |
| `source` | `DeferredDeepLinkSource` | `clipboard`, `referrer` or `fingerprint`: which signal produced the answer |
| `confidenceScore` | `double` | `0`–`100`. Server score for fingerprint results, `100` for clipboard and referrer |
| `matchQuality` | `MatchQuality` | `HIGH` 75+, `MEDIUM` 50–74, `LOW` 30–49 |
| `deeplinkId`, `targetUrl`, `campaignId`, `metadata`, `matchedAt`, `expiresAt` | optional | From the server |
| `matchDetails` | `MatchDetails?` | Score breakdown (fingerprint results) |

A `QueryValue` is one of:

- `SingleQueryValue` for `?ref=newsletter`
- `FlagQueryValue` for `?debug` or `?debug=`
- `MultipleQueryValue` for a repeated key, `?tag=a&tag=b`

Use `.stringValue` for the common case (`link.queryParams['ref']?.stringValue`), `.stringValues` for lists, or switch on the type.

## How fingerprint matching works

- The landing page stores a small description of the click: IP address, device class, OS version, screen size, language, time zone, and the path and query that were tapped.
- The SDK sends the same kind of description of the device. The server compares it with clicks on your app's link pages from the **last 1 hour** and returns up to 10 candidates, best first, each with a `confidence_score` (0–100) and a `match_quality` (`HIGH`, `MEDIUM`, `LOW`). Candidates below 30 are not returned.
- An IP match is not required (iCloud Private Relay and carrier NAT often change the IP between browser and app).
- Missing data never counts as agreement, and the time score decays linearly across the 1-hour claim window.
- **You choose the threshold.** `minConfidence` is off by default. Use `matchQuality` or `confidenceScore` to decide what to route automatically and what to confirm with the user.

## Handling links that open the app

When the app is already installed, a tap on your link opens it directly (Universal Link / App Link). Receive the URL with a package such as [`app_links`](https://pub.dev/packages/app_links), then parse it with the same rules as the deferred result:

```dart
final parsed = await DeepLinkNow.parseDeepLink(uri.toString());
if (parsed != null) router.go(parsed.fullPath);
```

`parseDeepLink(url)` returns `{path, queryParams, fullPath, url}`, or `null` for URLs that are not on your link domains (exactly `<alias>.deeplinknow.com` or your verified custom domain). It returns a `Future` because Flutter platform channels are asynchronous; the parse itself runs in the native SDK.

### iOS apps on the UIScene lifecycle (Flutter 3.41+ by default)

If links that open the installed app never reach your Dart code on iOS, check these:

1. **Use `app_links` 7.0.0 or later.** Flutter 3.38 added UIScene support, Flutter 3.41 turns it on by default (and migrates an unmodified app delegate automatically), and apps built with Xcode 27 must use it. Once your app is on UIScene, iOS delivers links to the scene delegate, not the app delegate. `app_links` 6.x only hooks the app-delegate callbacks, so links never reach Dart and nothing reports an error. 7.0.0 added UISceneDelegate support. The same applies to any plugin that only calls `addApplicationDelegate`.
2. **Set `FlutterDeepLinkingEnabled` to `false`** in `ios/Runner/Info.plist` when a plugin handles your links. Otherwise the engine hands links it doesn't claim back to iOS, and the user bounces from the app to Safari and back.
3. **Subscribe to `uriLinkStream` synchronously at the top of `initState`**, before any `await`. The stream doesn't replay links that arrived before you subscribed. Queue the link until your startup is ready.
4. **Put a timeout on every external `await` in startup** (for example `FirebaseMessaging.getInitialMessage()`), and drain the link queue in a `finally` block, so one slow call can't hold the link forever.

## API

All members are static on `DeepLinkNow`.

| Member | Returns | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `initialize(apiKey, {config})` | `Future<DLNAppInfo?>` | One native init. `null` on failure, never throws |
| `isInitialized` | `bool` | Whether the last `initialize` succeeded |
| `appInfo` | `DLNAppInfo?` | App id, alias, link domains, primary domain |
| `checkDeferredDeepLink({minConfidence, useClipboard, force})` | `Future<DeferredDeepLink?>` | `null` = no link or failure; never throws |
| `resetDeferredDeepLink()` | `Future<void>` | Clears the first-launch state, for testing |
| `findDeferredUser()` | `Future<MatchResponse?>` | Every fingerprint candidate from `/api/v1/sdk/match`, in server order, as typed classes. `null` on failure |
| `getReferrerData()` | `Future<ReferrerData?>` | Android only: the raw Install Referrer result. `null` on iOS |
| `checkClipboard()` | `Future<String?>` | The clipboard text if it is one of your links. May show the iOS paste prompt |
| `hasDeepLinkToken()` | `Future<bool>` | Cheap check that shows no paste prompt |
| `parseDeepLink(url)` | `Future<ParsedDeepLink?>` | Validate and parse a URL on your link domains |
| `isValidDomain(host)` | `Future<bool>` | Whether the host is one of your link domains |
| `lastError` | `DLNError?` | Last failure of `initialize`, `checkDeferredDeepLink` or `findDeferredUser` |
| `sdkVersion` | `String` | `"1.3.0"` |

Not in the Flutter plugin: a link stream for direct opens (use `app_links`) and `createDeepLink`. Web, macOS, Windows and Linux aren't supported: there, every call resolves `null` or `false` and `lastError` is `notInitialized`.

## FlutterFlow

Add `deeplinknow: ^1.3.0` under a custom action's **Pubspec Dependencies**. The [FlutterFlow guide](/docs/flutterflow) has the custom action that opens the right FlutterFlow page from the link, plus the entitlement and intent filter steps in FlutterFlow's Configuration Files.

## Testing your integration

- A link is delivered once per install. To try again without reinstalling, call `DeepLinkNow.resetDeferredDeepLink()` or pass `force: true`.
- iOS: open your link in Safari on the device, tap the App Store button (this copies the link), then run the app from Xcode.
- Android: test the Install Referrer with an internal test track install from a link. A sideloaded build has no referrer and falls back to fingerprint matching.
- `DLNConfig(enableLogs: true)` turns on the native debug logs (`[DeepLinkNow]` in the Xcode console, tag `DLN` in Logcat). The API key is never logged.
- Universal Links not opening the app: check Apple's CDN copy of your association file at `https://app-site-association.cdn-apple.com/a/v1/<your domain>`, or run the free [AASA validator](/tools/aasa-validator).
- `lastError` says "native plugin is not available": stop the app and rebuild it after adding the package.

## Privacy

The plugin adds nothing to what the native SDKs collect: the device fields used for matching (platform, OS version, device model, screen size, language, time zone, an app-scoped install ID), sent only to DeepLinkNow, and no advertising identifiers. It adds no Android permissions. See the [iOS](/docs/ios) and [Android](/docs/android) docs for the App Store privacy labels and the Play Data safety form.

## API endpoints used

| Endpoint | Key | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/v1/sdk/init` | public | `initialize` (one call per `initialize`) |
| `GET /api/v1/sdk/referrer-lookup` | public | `checkDeferredDeepLink` on Android |
| `POST /api/v1/sdk/match` | public | `checkDeferredDeepLink` (fingerprint step), `findDeferredUser` |

## Support

- Email: support@deeplinknow.com
- Package: [pub.dev/packages/deeplinknow](https://pub.dev/packages/deeplinknow)
