Source: https://deeplinknow.com/docs/flutterflow

# Deferred deep links in FlutterFlow

Send people to the right page of your FlutterFlow app from any link, including after they install it from the App Store or Google Play. You add one custom action, paste one file, and set one On Page Load action.

A DeepLinkNow link's path is a FlutterFlow route. `https://yourapp.deeplinknow.com/productPage?productId=42` opens the page whose route is `/productPage`, with its `productId` parameter set to 42. There's nothing to create in a dashboard first: every path on your link domain works.

## Before you start

- A DeepLinkNow account (free up to 25,000 monthly active users) and an app created in the dashboard.
- Your iOS Team ID and Bundle ID, and your Android package name and Play signing SHA-256 certificate. The dashboard's setup page says where to find each one, and fills most of them in from your App Store or Play link.
- A build on a real phone to test. Deep links don't run in FlutterFlow's Run or Test mode, because the plugin has no web version.

## 1. Set up your app in DeepLinkNow

1. In the dashboard, open your app's setup page (or **Settings › iOS** and **Settings › Android**) and fill in the Team ID, Bundle ID and App Store ID, and the package name and SHA-256 certificate.
2. Open **Settings › API keys** and copy the **public** key (`dln_pub_…`). It's safe to put in your app.

Your link domain is `<alias>.deeplinknow.com`, shown on the app's Overview.

## 2. Add the custom action

1. In FlutterFlow, open **Custom Code** and add an **Action** named `dlnOpenDeferredLink`.
2. In its settings:
   - turn on **Include BuildContext**;
   - add one argument, `publicKey`, of type **String**;
   - set the return value to **String**, nullable;
   - under **Pubspec Dependencies**, add `deeplinknow: ^1.3.0`.
3. Keep the automatic imports FlutterFlow puts at the top of the file, and replace everything below `// DO NOT REMOVE OR MODIFY THE CODE ABOVE!` with:

```dart
import 'package:deeplinknow/deeplinknow.dart';
import 'package:go_router/go_router.dart';

/// Opens the page for the link the user tapped before installing, and
/// returns the location it opened (or null). Add it as the first On Page
/// Load action of your entry page. The link's path is a FlutterFlow route:
/// /productPage?productId=42 opens the page whose route is /productPage.
Future<String?> dlnOpenDeferredLink(
  BuildContext context,
  String publicKey,
) async {
  if (!DeepLinkNow.isInitialized) {
    final info = await DeepLinkNow.initialize(publicKey);
    if (info == null) return null;
  }
  final link = await DeepLinkNow.checkDeferredDeepLink();
  if (link == null || !context.mounted) return null;

  var value = link.fullPath.trim();
  if (value.isEmpty) return null;
  if (!value.startsWith('/')) value = '/$value';
  final queryAt = value.indexOf('?');
  var path = queryAt < 0 ? value : value.substring(0, queryAt);
  var query = queryAt < 0 ? '' : value.substring(queryAt);
  if (query == '?') query = '';
  while (path.length > 1 && path.endsWith('/')) {
    path = path.substring(0, path.length - 1);
  }
  if (path == '/' && query.isEmpty) return null;

  final location = '$path$query';
  context.push(location);
  return location;
}
```

4. Save and compile. `go_router` is already part of every FlutterFlow project.

## 3. Run it on the entry page

1. Open your app's entry page (the first page people see).
2. In **Actions › On Page Load**, add **Custom Action › dlnOpenDeferredLink** as the first action, and set `publicKey` to your public key.

The first time the app opens after an install, the action asks DeepLinkNow which link the person tapped and opens that page. A link to `/`, or no link, leaves them on the entry page. Every later launch skips the check without a network call.

A page's route is under the page's settings. Page parameters come from the link's query string, so a page with a `productId` parameter reads it from `?productId=42`.

## 4. Open the installed app from links

For a tap to open the app when it's already installed, iOS and Android need to know your app owns the link domain. In each snippet, replace `yourapp.deeplinknow.com` with your link domain.

1. **Settings › App Details › Deep Linking**: turn deep linking on.
2. **Custom Code › Configuration Files › Runner.entitlements**: add

```xml
<key>com.apple.developer.associated-domains</key>
<array>
  <string>applinks:yourapp.deeplinknow.com</string>
</array>
```

3. **Custom Code › Configuration Files › AndroidManifest.xml**, in **Activity Tags**: add

```xml
<intent-filter android:autoVerify="true">
  <action android:name="android.intent.action.VIEW" />
  <category android:name="android.intent.category.DEFAULT" />
  <category android:name="android.intent.category.BROWSABLE" />
  <data android:scheme="https" android:host="yourapp.deeplinknow.com" />
</intent-filter>
```

4. In the Apple Developer portal, open your App ID under **Certificates, Identifiers & Profiles** and turn on **Associated Domains**.

If you add a custom domain in DeepLinkNow later, add it to both snippets and release an update.

## 5. Test it

1. Delete the app from your phone.
2. On the phone, tap a link such as `https://yourapp.deeplinknow.com/productPage?productId=42`. The link page sends you to the store.
3. Install your build (TestFlight, an internal test track, or a local run) and open it. It lands on the product page.

To test again without reinstalling, add a second custom action, `dlnResetDeferredLink` (no arguments, no return value, the same dependency), call it from a debug-only button, then restart the app:

```dart
import 'package:deeplinknow/deeplinknow.dart';

/// For testing only: the next dlnOpenDeferredLink asks again, as after a
/// fresh install.
Future dlnResetDeferredLink() async {
  try {
    await DeepLinkNow.resetDeferredDeepLink();
  } catch (_) {
    // Already logged by the SDK.
  }
}
```

## Troubleshooting

- **Nothing opens.** Check the device logs for `[DeepLinkNow]` (iOS) or `DLN` (Android). An invalid key, or an app with no App Store ID or package name, shows up there.
- **It opens the wrong page, or an error page.** The link's path has to match a page's route exactly, including case.
- **Taps open the browser instead of the installed app.** Check your domain with the [AASA validator](/tools/aasa-validator) and the [assetlinks validator](/tools/assetlinks-validator), and that Associated Domains is on for the App ID.
- **Coming from Branch?** The [switch check](/tools/switch-check) shows how your existing links move.

The plugin underneath is [`deeplinknow` on pub.dev](https://pub.dev/packages/deeplinknow); the [Flutter SDK docs](/docs/flutter) cover the rest of its API.

---
Source: https://deeplinknow.com/docs/mcp

# DeepLinkNow MCP server for coding agents

## Overview

[`@deeplinknow/mcp`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@deeplinknow/mcp) is an MCP server for coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor, Claude Desktop, VS Code and Windsurf. With it installed, the agent can read DeepLinkNow's current docs, check your link domain and plan a migration while it writes the integration, instead of working from memory.

It covers iOS, Android, React Native, Expo and Flutter apps. Like DeepLinkNow itself, it does deep linking only: it never adds attribution, ad tracking or advertising IDs to your app.

The server runs on your machine over stdio and needs Node.js 20 or later. The source is MIT licensed: [github.com/deeplinknow/dln-mcp](https://github.com/deeplinknow/dln-mcp).

## Install

<!-- slot:quick-install -->
One-click install, with no key: [Add to Cursor](https://cursor.com/install-mcp?name=deeplinknow&config=eyJjb21tYW5kIjoibnB4IC15IEBkZWVwbGlua25vdy9tY3AifQ%3D%3D) · [Install in VS Code](https://insiders.vscode.dev/redirect?url=vscode%3Amcp%2Finstall%3F%257B%2522name%2522%253A%2522deeplinknow%2522%252C%2522command%2522%253A%2522npx%2522%252C%2522args%2522%253A%255B%2522-y%2522%252C%2522%2540deeplinknow%252Fmcp%2522%255D%257D). Claude Code: `claude mcp add deeplinknow -- npx -y @deeplinknow/mcp`.
<!-- /slot:quick-install -->

<!-- slot:try-it -->
Once it's installed, try asking your agent:

- "Use DeepLinkNow to add deferred deep linking to this Expo app. Our link domain is myapp.deeplinknow.com." (`get_setup_guide`)
- "Check whether links.example.com's AASA and assetlinks.json files are set up correctly." (`check_domain`)
- "We use Firebase Dynamic Links. Plan our move to DeepLinkNow for this app." (`migrate_from`)
- "A DeepLinkNow match came back MEDIUM with a score of 58. Should we route it?" (`explain_match_result`)
- "Search the DeepLinkNow docs: how do I test a deferred deep link on Android?" (`search_docs`)
<!-- /slot:try-it -->

The one-click links and the commands above install the server without a key. To add the private key for the link tools, use the per-client configs below.

### Claude Code

```sh
claude mcp add deeplinknow -- npx -y @deeplinknow/mcp
```

With the link tools (`--scope user` keeps the key out of the project's `.mcp.json`):

```sh
claude mcp add deeplinknow --scope user --env DEEPLINKNOW_API_KEY=YOUR_PRIVATE_KEY -- npx -y @deeplinknow/mcp
```

### Cursor

Add to `.cursor/mcp.json` in the project, or `~/.cursor/mcp.json` for every project:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "deeplinknow": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@deeplinknow/mcp"],
      "env": { "DEEPLINKNOW_API_KEY": "${env:DEEPLINKNOW_API_KEY}" }
    }
  }
}
```

Leave out `env` if you don't need the link tools.

### Claude Desktop

Open **Settings → Developer → Edit Config**, which opens `claude_desktop_config.json` (`~/Library/Application Support/Claude/` on macOS, `%APPDATA%\Claude\` on Windows), and add:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "deeplinknow": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@deeplinknow/mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

Restart Claude Desktop. To use the link tools, add `"env": { "DEEPLINKNOW_API_KEY": "YOUR_PRIVATE_KEY" }` next to `args`.

### VS Code

Add to `.vscode/mcp.json`. VS Code asks for the key once and stores it securely:

```json
{
  "inputs": [
    {
      "type": "promptString",
      "id": "deeplinknow-api-key",
      "description": "DeepLinkNow private API key (dln_priv_…), only for list_links and create_link. Leave empty otherwise.",
      "password": true
    }
  ],
  "servers": {
    "deeplinknow": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@deeplinknow/mcp"],
      "env": { "DEEPLINKNOW_API_KEY": "${input:deeplinknow-api-key}" }
    }
  }
}
```

### Windsurf

Add to `~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "deeplinknow": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@deeplinknow/mcp"],
      "env": { "DEEPLINKNOW_API_KEY": "YOUR_PRIVATE_KEY" }
    }
  }
}
```

Leave out `env` if you don't need the link tools.

### Other clients

Any MCP client that runs stdio servers: command `npx`, arguments `-y @deeplinknow/mcp`.

## What to ask

```text
Add DeepLinkNow deferred deep linking to this app. Our link domain is myapp.deeplinknow.com.
```

The agent reads the setup guide for your platform, installs the SDK, adds the Associated Domains entitlement and the Android intent filter, calls `checkDeferredDeepLink()` on launch and routes the result through your router. Then it checks your domain.

Other requests it handles:

- "Check myapp.deeplinknow.com" (or your custom domain). It validates `apple-app-site-association` against Apple's CDN copy and `assetlinks.json` against Google's Digital Asset Links API, and looks the domain up on the EasyPrivacy and AdGuard block lists. It works for any domain, including the one you use today.
- "We're on Firebase Dynamic Links. Move us to DeepLinkNow." Branch, AppsFlyer and Adjust work too. You get a plan and a code diff for your platform. If you use one of those for attribution, the plan keeps it for that and moves only the deep links.
- "This match came back MEDIUM with a score of 58. Should we route it?" The agent explains each part of the score and what a `minConfidence` of 50 or 75 would do. The threshold stays your decision.

## Tools

| Tool | Needs a key | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `get_setup_guide` | No | Setup steps and code for `ios`, `android`, `react-native`, `expo` or `flutter`, from these docs (a bundled copy when offline) |
| `search_docs` | No | Searches the full DeepLinkNow docs and returns the matching sections with links |
| `check_domain` | No | Checks a domain's `apple-app-site-association` (and Apple's CDN copy), `assetlinks.json` (and Google's verdict), and whether the domain or its CNAME chain is on the EasyPrivacy or AdGuard block lists |
| `explain_match_result` | No | Explains a fingerprint match's `confidence_score` and `match_quality`, and how to choose `minConfidence` |
| `migrate_from` | No | A migration plan and code diff from `firebase-dynamic-links`, `branch`, `appsflyer` or `adjust` |
| `list_links` | Private key, paid plan | Lists the app's links (dashboard, API and on-demand), with search and paging |
| `create_link` | Private key, paid plan | Creates a link with a custom path, link-page text, social preview, metadata or campaign |

It also exposes `deeplinknow://llms.txt` and `deeplinknow://docs/{page}` as resources, and two prompts: `add_deferred_deep_linking` and `migrate_to_deeplinknow`.

The first `check_domain` run downloads the block lists (about 22 MB). Later checks in the same session reuse them for a day.

## Keys

You don't need an account or a key for the first five tools.

`list_links` and `create_link` call the [management API](/docs/api/deeplinks), which needs your app's **private** key (`dln_priv_…`, from the app's API Keys page in the dashboard) as `DEEPLINKNOW_API_KEY`. The management API is on paid plans ([pricing](/pricing)). A private key acts on one app.

You never have to create links: any path on your link domain already works. The link tools are for listing links, or for creating one with a custom preview or campaign.

The private key stays in your MCP config. Your app only ever contains the public key (`dln_pub_…`). The server refuses a public key for the link tools without sending it, and it never prints, logs or returns the private key: it sends it only in the `x-api-key` header to the DeepLinkNow API.

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `DEEPLINKNOW_API_KEY` | unset | Your app's private key, only for `list_links` and `create_link` |
| `DEEPLINKNOW_API_URL` | `https://deeplinknow.com` | API base URL. Must be https (http only for localhost) |

## What it doesn't do

- It never writes files or runs commands. The server only returns text to the agent. Your agent makes the code changes, through its own tools and permission prompts.
- It stores nothing on disk. Docs, block lists and check results are cached in memory while the server runs (docs for an hour, block lists for a day, domain results for 5 minutes).
- No telemetry: it collects no usage data.
- It sends nothing about your code. `get_setup_guide`, `search_docs`, `migrate_from` and the resources fetch public docs from `https://deeplinknow.com`. `check_domain` fetches only the domain you name (over https, refusing private and local addresses), Apple's CDN, Google's Digital Asset Links API and the four public block lists. `explain_match_result` makes no requests. Only the link tools send your key and the link fields, to the DeepLinkNow API.

## Keep agents on track

Paste this into your repo's `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` so every session follows the same rules:

```markdown
## Deep linking: DeepLinkNow

- Link domain: myapp.deeplinknow.com. Any path and query on it is a deep link; nothing has to be created first.
- The app contains only the public key (dln_pub_…). Never commit or ship the private key.
- Initialize once at launch. Call checkDeferredDeepLink() once on launch and route to link.path with link.queryParams. Send links that open the installed app through the SDK's parse method and the same router.
- Fingerprint matches are scored (confidenceScore, matchQuality). minConfidence is off by default; decide how to treat MEDIUM and LOW.
- Use the DeepLinkNow MCP tools (get_setup_guide, check_domain, search_docs) instead of guessing.
```

## Support

- Email: support@deeplinknow.com
- Package: [npmjs.com/package/@deeplinknow/mcp](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@deeplinknow/mcp)
- Source: [github.com/deeplinknow/dln-mcp](https://github.com/deeplinknow/dln-mcp)

# Migrating from Firebase Dynamic Links

Firebase Dynamic Links shut down on 25 August 2025: every `page.link` URL now returns a 404, and the `.page.link` domains are gone. Nobody can bring those URLs back, DeepLinkNow included. This guide moves the *behaviour* to DeepLinkNow: links that open your app if it's installed, survive an install if it isn't, and hand your app the original link on first launch.

There are two ways to do it. Pick one, or start with the first and move to the second over time.

## Option 1: keep your long links, change the host

If you built Dynamic Links in code as long links, like

```
https://yourapp.page.link/?link=https%3A%2F%2Fyourapp.com%2Finvite%2F8Fk2&apn=com.yourapp&ibi=com.yourapp.ios
```

the same URL works on your DeepLinkNow domain with only the host changed:

```
https://yourapp.deeplinknow.com/?link=https%3A%2F%2Fyourapp.com%2Finvite%2F8Fk2&apn=com.yourapp&ibi=com.yourapp.ios
```

DeepLinkNow accepts any path and query on your domain without creating links first, and passes the query through untouched. Your app gets the Firebase-style `link` parameter back, already decoded, in `queryParams.link`, both when the link opens the installed app and after an install.

All long links on `/` count as **one** link against your plan's link limit, because the limit counts distinct paths and ignores the query string.

What's different from Firebase:

- `apn`, `ibi`, `isi` and `efr` aren't needed. DeepLinkNow knows your app from the domain, and it sends users to the App Store or Google Play listing you set in the dashboard. They're harmless to leave in.
- `afl`, `ifl` and `ofl` (fallback URLs) aren't followed. Phones go to the store; desktop shows a QR code and store buttons.
- `st`, `sd` and `si` (social preview) aren't read from the URL. Set the preview title, description and image in the dashboard (paid plans).
- Short links (`yourapp.page.link/abc`) have no equivalent code to keep: use a path instead (Option 2). If your short links were on your own domain, you can import them (see below).

### React Native

Before (`@react-native-firebase/dynamic-links`):

```typescript
const initial = await dynamicLinks().getInitialLink();
if (initial) handle(initial.url);
dynamicLinks().onLink((link) => handle(link.url));
```

After (`@deeplinknow/react-native`):

```typescript
import DeepLinkNow from "@deeplinknow/react-native";
import { Linking } from "react-native";

await DeepLinkNow.initialize("dln_pub_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx");

const linkParam = (q: Record<string, unknown>) =>
  typeof q.link === "string" ? q.link : null;

// After an install: the link the user tapped before installing.
const deferred = await DeepLinkNow.checkDeferredDeepLink();
const fromInstall = deferred && linkParam(deferred.queryParams);
if (fromInstall) handle(fromInstall);

// App already installed: the Universal Link / App Link that opened it.
const onUrl = (url: string | null) => {
  const parsed = url ? DeepLinkNow.parseDeepLink(url) : null;
  const value = parsed && linkParam(parsed.queryParams);
  if (value) handle(value);
};
Linking.getInitialURL().then(onUrl);
Linking.addEventListener("url", ({ url }) => onUrl(url));
```

### iOS (Swift)

```swift
import DeepLinkNow

await DeepLinkNow.initialize(config: DLNConfig(apiKey: "dln_pub_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"))

// After an install
if let deferred = await DeepLinkNow.checkDeferredDeepLink(),
   let value = deferred.queryParams["link"]?.stringValue {
    handle(URL(string: value))
}

// App already installed (SwiftUI)
.onOpenURL { url in
    if let link = DeepLinkNow.parseLink(url),
       let value = link.queryParams["link"]?.stringValue {
        handle(URL(string: value))
    }
}
```

### Android (Kotlin)

```kotlin
// After an install (inside a coroutine; it returns a Result and never throws)
DLN.checkDeferredDeepLink().onSuccess { deferred ->
    (deferred?.queryParams?.get("link") as? QueryValue.Single)?.value?.let(::handle)
}

// App already installed (onCreate and onNewIntent)
intent.data?.toString()?.let { url ->
    DLN.parseDeepLink(url)?.let { link ->
        (link.queryParams["link"] as? QueryValue.Single)?.value?.let(::handle)
    }
}
```

## Option 2: put the path in the link

Firebase needed the `link=` wrapper because `page.link` wasn't your domain. On DeepLinkNow it is. Instead of wrapping `https://yourapp.com/invite/8Fk2`, use the path directly:

```
https://yourapp.deeplinknow.com/invite/8Fk2
```

Your app gets `path: "/invite/8Fk2"` and any query parameters, and routes on them. This is shorter, reads better in a message, and works with your own domain (`go.yourapp.com/invite/8Fk2`) on paid plans.

Each distinct path counts once against your link limit, so put per-user values in the query (`/invite?code=8Fk2`) if you generate a lot of them.

## Import your old short links

If your Dynamic Links used your own domain (such as `links.yourapp.com`) rather than `page.link`, the short links people already shared can keep working. Point that domain at DeepLinkNow as your app's custom domain, then import the links Firebase let you export.

1. Export your Dynamic Links with Google Takeout. You get one CSV file per domain.
2. In the dashboard, open your app's **Deep Links** page and choose **Import from Firebase**.
3. Choose the CSV files. The preview shows how many links each file holds, which domains they use, and any rows that can't be imported.
4. Choose **Import**. When it finishes you can download the rows that weren't imported as a CSV, fix them and import that file again.

Each short link becomes a link on the same path, so `https://links.yourapp.com/abc123` is stored as `abc123`. Its target URL is the original Firebase deep link, its link name becomes the title, and the social title, description and image carry over. The other Firebase parameters (`apn`, `ibi`, `utm_source` and so on) are kept in the link's metadata under `fdl`.

When someone taps an imported link and installs your app, the deferred result carries the original deep link in `targetUrl`. When the app is already installed, the link opens it directly without reaching DeepLinkNow, so look the path up yourself:

```typescript
const res = await fetch(
  `https://deeplinknow.com/api/v1/sdk/resolve?path=${encodeURIComponent("/abc123")}`,
  { headers: { "x-api-key": "dln_pub_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx" } }
);
if (res.ok) {
  const { deeplink } = await res.json();
  handle(deeplink.target_url);
}
```

A path your app already has is skipped, never overwritten. Every imported link counts toward your plan's link limit, and links past it are reported so you can import them again after upgrading. Archived links are left out unless you ask for them.

## Checklist

1. Create the app in the DeepLinkNow dashboard and enter your iOS Team ID and Bundle ID and your Android package name and SHA-256 fingerprints. DeepLinkNow serves `apple-app-site-association` and `assetlinks.json` for your domain.
2. Add `applinks:yourapp.deeplinknow.com` to Associated Domains (iOS) and an `autoVerify` https intent filter for it (Android). With Expo, the config plugin does both.
3. Replace the Firebase Dynamic Links SDK calls as shown above, and remove the `firebase_dynamic_links` / `@react-native-firebase/dynamic-links` dependency.
4. Change the host in the code that builds links (Option 1), or switch to paths (Option 2).
5. Check your domain with the free [deep link domain checker](/tools).

## What DeepLinkNow doesn't replace

- Old `page.link` URLs no longer work. Update links you control (emails, QR codes, your site), and accept that old shared links won't open.
- Firebase Auth email-link sign-in used Dynamic Links for the sign-in email; Firebase's own documentation covers moving that flow off Dynamic Links. DeepLinkNow doesn't handle sign-in links.
- Firebase reported clicks into Google Analytics. DeepLinkNow shows click and install counts, and hands your app the link so you can send it to your own analytics.

Source: https://deeplinknow.com/docs/integration-checklist

# Integration checklist

An end-to-end checklist for integrating DeepLinkNow into your mobile app.

## Dashboard setup

### Account and app

- [ ] Create a DeepLinkNow account and an app in the dashboard
- [ ] Choose your app alias (e.g. `myapp` → `myapp.deeplinknow.com`)
- [ ] Copy your keys from the **API Keys** page. Each app gets one **public** key (`dln_pub_…`, for the SDKs) and one **private** key (`dln_priv_…`, for your server only). The public key is always shown there. The private key is shown once; regenerate it there if you lose it, and choose how long the old one keeps working (24 hours by default, or immediately if it leaked).
- [ ] Optional: configure a fallback URL for desktop visitors

### iOS settings

- [ ] Bundle ID (e.g. `com.company.myapp`)
- [ ] Team ID / App ID prefix (from your Apple Developer account)
- [ ] App Store ID (once the app is published)

### Android settings

- [ ] Package name (e.g. `com.company.myapp`)
- [ ] SHA-256 certificate fingerprints: Play App Signing, upload key and debug (`keytool -list -v -keystore ~/.android/debug.keystore`)

### Verify the .well-known files

- [ ] `https://myapp.deeplinknow.com/.well-known/apple-app-site-association` contains your Team ID and Bundle ID
- [ ] `https://myapp.deeplinknow.com/.well-known/assetlinks.json` contains your package name and fingerprints

These files are served from your saved settings and cached for up to 5 minutes.

## SDK installation

- [ ] **React Native / Expo**: `npx expo install @deeplinknow/react-native` (development build, not Expo Go) or `npm install @deeplinknow/react-native` + `pod install`
- [ ] **iOS**: `pod 'DeepLinkNow', '~> 1.3'` or Swift Package Manager `https://github.com/deeplinknow/dln-ios`
- [ ] **Android**: `implementation("com.deeplinknow:dln-android:1.3.0")` (the library declares `INTERNET` itself)
- [ ] **Flutter**: `flutter pub add deeplinknow` (iOS 13+, Android `minSdk` 24; rebuild the app after adding it)
- [ ] iOS: Associated Domains `applinks:myapp.deeplinknow.com` (and your custom domain)
- [ ] Android: `autoVerify` https intent filter for `myapp.deeplinknow.com` (and your custom domain)
- [ ] No ATT prompt, IDFA, or advertising-ID permission is needed for DeepLinkNow

## Initialization

- [ ] Initialize once at app start with your **public** key (`dln_pub_…`)
- [ ] Never ship your private key in an app
- [ ] Handle an initialization failure (invalid key, inactive account, offline) separately from "no deferred link"
- [ ] Use `enableLogs` only in development builds

## Deferred deep linking

- [ ] Call `checkDeferredDeepLink()` once on launch, after initialization
- [ ] Route to `link.path` with `link.queryParams` when it returns a link
- [ ] Decide your threshold for fingerprint results. Every result carries `confidenceScore` (0–100) and `matchQuality` (`HIGH` 75+, `MEDIUM` 50–74, `LOW` 30–49). The optional `minConfidence` filter is off by default.
- [ ] Consider confirming `MEDIUM` or `LOW` fingerprint matches with the user before routing
- [ ] iOS: decide whether to keep the pasteboard step (`useClipboard`, default `true`), which can show the iOS 16+ paste prompt
- [ ] Treat errors as "try again later", not as "no link". The SDK retries on the next call.

## Links that open the installed app

- [ ] Pass incoming Universal Links / App Links to `parseDeepLink(url)`
- [ ] Route deferred and direct links through the same function

```typescript
function route(path: string, query: Record<string, string | true | string[]>) {
  switch (path) {
    case "/product":
      navigation.navigate("Product", { id: query.id });
      break;
    case "/category":
      navigation.navigate("Category", { name: query.name });
      break;
    default:
      navigation.navigate("Home");
  }
}
```

- [ ] Handle unknown paths gracefully

## Testing

### Direct links

- [ ] Tap `https://myapp.deeplinknow.com/product?id=123` from Notes or Messages with the app installed: the app opens on the right screen
- [ ] Android: `adb shell pm get-app-links <your.package>` shows your domains as verified

### Deferred links

- [ ] Uninstall the app, tap a link, install, open: the app lands on the right screen
- [ ] iOS: test both **Allow** and **Don't Allow** on the paste prompt (Don't Allow falls back to fingerprint matching)
- [ ] Android: test an install through the link's Play Store button (Install Referrer) and one without it (fingerprint)
- [ ] Check the logs for each step's outcome, `source`, `confidenceScore` and `matchQuality`
- [ ] Use `resetDeferredDeepLink()` or `force: true` to repeat the test without reinstalling
- [ ] A click older than 1 hour is not offered as a fingerprint match

### Edge cases

- [ ] First launch offline: no crash, and the next launch still finds the link
- [ ] Unknown path: falls back to a sensible screen
- [ ] A link copied from another app's domain is ignored

## Production readiness

- [ ] Only the public key is in the app binary
- [ ] Logging is off in release builds
- [ ] `.well-known` files are correct for your release signing certificates
- [ ] Privacy labels: the SDKs collect device characteristics and an app-scoped install ID for app functionality only, not for tracking

## Optional

- [ ] Custom domain (paid plans): add it under **Domains**, create the DNS record, wait for verification, then add it to Associated Domains and your intent filters
- [ ] Customize the landing page (title, subtitle, button text, social preview)
- [ ] Forward deferred-link events to your own analytics tool (DeepLinkNow does not do analytics)

## Need help?

- [Quick Start](/docs/quickstart)
- [iOS](/docs/ios), [Android](/docs/android), [React Native](/docs/react-native), [Flutter](/docs/flutter)
- [MCP server for coding agents](/docs/mcp)
- Email: support@deeplinknow.com

Source: https://deeplinknow.com/docs/smart-banner

# Smart banner

Show phone visitors of your website a bar that opens the page they're on in your app, or sends them to the store if they don't have it yet. It's one script tag, it makes no other request, and it sets no cookie. Smart banners are included on Startup and higher plans, and in the free trial.

## Set it up

1. In the dashboard, open your app's **Settings › Smart banner**.
2. Turn on **Show the banner** and list the websites it may show on, one per line, exactly as they appear in the address bar: `https://www.example.com`. Add `https://example.com` too if your site answers on both. For local testing, `http://localhost:3000` works.
3. Optionally change the title, subtitle and button text. Blank fields use your link page's title and subtitle, then "Continue in the app" and "Open".
4. Pick where it sits, how long it stays hidden after a visitor closes it, and which link the button opens. Save.
5. Copy the tag for your link domain and paste it into every page of your site, in `<head>` or before `</body>`:

```html
<script async src="https://myapp.deeplinknow.com/.well-known/dln/open.js" referrerpolicy="no-referrer"></script>
```

If your app has a custom domain, the dashboard shows a tag for it as well (for example `https://links.example.com/.well-known/dln/open.js`). Use that one to keep everything on your own domains.

Changes you save reach your site within 5 minutes, because the script is cached for that long.

## What visitors see

The bar shows in Safari, Chrome and other browsers on iPhone, iPad and Android, on the websites you listed. It doesn't show on desktop, inside an app's own web view, or on any other site that copies your tag.

At the top, the bar sits above your page in the page flow, so it pushes the content down and scrolls away with it. At the bottom, it stays fixed above the home indicator, and the script adds the same height of space at the end of your page so nothing stays hidden behind it.

It follows the visitor's light or dark mode and skips the slide-in animation when they've asked for reduced motion. The icon is your app icon when that file is 48 KB or smaller (a 128 × 128 PNG is plenty); otherwise the bar shows your app's first two letters.

## Which link the button opens

By default the button opens the same path and query on your link domain. A visitor on

```
https://www.example.com/products/123?ref=newsletter
```

taps through to

```
https://myapp.deeplinknow.com/products/123?ref=newsletter
```

If the app is installed, Universal Links and App Links open it on that path. If it isn't, the link page sends the visitor to the App Store or Play Store, and after install `checkDeferredDeepLink()` returns `/products/123` with `{ ref: "newsletter" }`. Your app handles it like any other DeepLinkNow link, so pages whose paths match your app's routes need no mapping.

If your website's paths don't match your app, choose **Always the same link** and enter one path, such as `/welcome`. Every page then opens that link.

The script never adds parameters to the link.

## Closing it

The close button hides the bar for the period you chose: until the tab is closed, a day, a week, or for good. That choice is the only thing the script stores, in the visitor's own browser under the key `dln-open:<your alias>`. If the browser blocks storage, the bar just shows again on the next page.

## Single-page apps

Back and forward navigation updates the bar on its own. After a client-side route change, call `refresh()` so the button points at the new page:

```js
window.DeepLinkNowBanner?.refresh();
```

`window.DeepLinkNowBanner?.hide()` removes the bar from the current page view without counting as a close. The object always exists once the tag has loaded, even when the banner is off for your plan or site, so these calls are safe anywhere.

In Next.js App Router, for example:

```tsx
"use client";
import { usePathname, useSearchParams } from "next/navigation";
import { useEffect } from "react";

export function RefreshAppBar() {
  const pathname = usePathname();
  const search = useSearchParams();
  useEffect(() => {
    (window as any).DeepLinkNowBanner?.refresh();
  }, [pathname, search]);
  return null;
}
```

## Privacy

The script tag is the only request. The script makes no network call of its own and sets no cookie. It reads the user agent to tell phones from desktops and stores the visitor's close, and that's all. DeepLinkNow doesn't count impressions. A tap is a normal visit to your link page and shows up in your link's click count like any other.

The tag's `referrerpolicy="no-referrer"` keeps your page's address out of the script request. Ad blockers have nothing to block: the script lives on your link domain under `/.well-known/`, and nothing in it looks like an ad or a tracker.

## Troubleshooting

- If nothing shows, check that you're on a phone (or a phone user agent), that the page's origin is in the list exactly (`https://www.example.com` and `https://example.com` are different sites), that the banner is on, and that you haven't closed it earlier. Clear the site's storage to see it again.
- With a Content Security Policy, allow your link domain in `script-src`, for example `script-src 'self' https://myapp.deeplinknow.com`. No other directive needs a change.
- If iOS shows two bars, the second is Safari's own Smart App Banner, from a `<meta name="apple-itunes-app">` tag. Remove that tag if you use this one.
- If the app opens on the wrong screen, remember the button passes the page's path. Handle that path in your app, or switch to **Always the same link**.
- If your own app shows your website in a web view, the bar stays hidden there as long as the web view keeps its default user agent. If your web view uses a browser-like user agent, call `window.DeepLinkNowBanner?.hide()` from it.

Source: https://deeplinknow.com/pricing

# DeepLinkNow pricing

Prices in USD. Startup, Growth and Scale are billed monthly, or yearly at 15% off: cancel any time, and paid plans keep their features until the end of the billing period. Enterprise is billed annually, by invoice.
No free trial is needed: the Developer plan is free, with no card.

## Developer: $0/month

Deep links and deferred deep links for one app, free.

- 25k SDK monthly active users
- 1k deep links (distinct paths, on-demand included)
- Single app on yourapp.deeplinknow.com
- Just you (1 seat)
- Universal Links, App Links and deferred deep links
- iOS, Android, React Native and Flutter SDKs
- Click and install counts
- Community support on Discord

## Startup: $49/month

Your own domain and a landing page that looks like your app.

- 100k SDK monthly active users
- 10k deep links (distinct paths, on-demand included)
- Custom domains: your links on go.yourapp.com (up to 3)
- Up to 3 apps
- Up to 3 team members, with admin and member roles
- Your branding on the link page
- Custom link page text and buttons, per app or per link
- Custom social previews for iMessage, Slack, WhatsApp and more
- Link page translated into 14 languages
- Link rules: allowed paths and a not-found redirect
- Android: skip the link page, straight to Google Play
- Fallback URL for visitors on a platform with no store listing
- Management API (10k requests/mo)
- Email support

For larger apps, or several apps under one account.

- 500k SDK monthly active users

- Unlimited custom domains
- Unlimited apps

- Everything in Startup
- Management API (50k requests/mo)
- Email support

For apps with millions of users, without a sales call or a contract.

- 2M SDK monthly active users

- Unlimited apps and custom domains
- Up to 10 team members
- Everything in Growth

For companies whose IT, legal and procurement teams have to sign off.

- Pay by invoice, against your purchase order

- Single sign-on with Microsoft Entra ID, Okta or Google Workspace, and SSO required for your domain

## Attribution platforms

Measurement platforms with deep links inside. If you need attribution, these are the real choice. If you don't, you pay for it anyway, in money, advertising IDs or both.

- [DeepLinkNow vs Branch](https://deeplinknow.com/compare/branch.md): Branch dropped its free tier. Custom domains start at $199/mo.
- [DeepLinkNow vs AppsFlyer](https://deeplinknow.com/compare/appsflyer.md): No deferred deep links on the free plan. Paid tiers need a sales call.
- [DeepLinkNow vs Adjust](https://deeplinknow.com/compare/adjust.md): Attribution first. Deferred links may be limited after an ATT opt-out.
- [DeepLinkNow vs Singular](https://deeplinknow.com/compare/singular.md): Free to 15,000 paid conversions. Every deep link is an attribution link.
- [DeepLinkNow vs Kochava](https://deeplinknow.com/compare/kochava.md): Free attribution with deferred links. Universal Links and your domain start at $500/mo.
- [DeepLinkNow vs Airbridge](https://deeplinknow.com/compare/airbridge.md): An MMP billed by data points: about $134/mo at 100,000 users.

## Developer-first deep linking tools

Smaller tools that do deep links without the full attribution suite, most of them started after Firebase Dynamic Links shut down.

- [DeepLinkNow vs Detour](https://deeplinknow.com/compare/detour.md): 1,500 free clicks, custom domains at $79/mo, and no match score in the app.
- [DeepLinkNow vs LinkTrace](https://deeplinknow.com/compare/linktrace.md): No SDK, fingerprint only, and no custom domain. Universal Links need its top plan.
- [DeepLinkNow vs AppsOnAir](https://deeplinknow.com/compare/appsonair.md): $54.97/mo for AppLink on your own domain, and no AppLink on the free plan.
- [DeepLinkNow vs URLgenius](https://deeplinknow.com/compare/urlgenius.md): Billed per click. Deferred links start at $199/mo on its Custom plan.

- [Firebase Dynamic Links alternative](https://deeplinknow.com/firebase-dynamic-links-alternative): Google shut it down on August 25, 2025. What DeepLinkNow does in its place, and what it doesn't.

DeepLinkNow is not affiliated with the vendors compared here.

# DeepLinkNow vs Branch

Deep linking and attribution platform. As of October 2026, with a public source for every claim.

I used Branch on a real startup. It worked, mostly, until the bill and the ad blockers showed up. Branch is a fine product if you're a marketing team that wants attribution and campaign analytics. If you just want a link to open the right screen after install, you're paying for a lot you'll never open.

| | DeepLinkNow | Branch | Stronger | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Free plan | Free for up to 25,000 monthly active users, deferred deep links included, and you don't need a card to start | There isn't one. The 30-day trial needs a work email and a card, then rolls onto Intro at $39/mo. | DeepLinkNow | [1] [2] |
| Usage over the plan | Links and SDK calls keep working, and I'll ask you to upgrade | Billed per extra volume credit, link and click, uncapped. | DeepLinkNow | [3] |
| Plan with a custom domain | $49/mo (Startup) | $199/mo (Activation Basics) | DeepLinkNow | [4] |
| iOS clipboard handoff | On every plan, including the free one | NativeLink, a premium feature | DeepLinkNow | [5] |
| Making links | Any path on your domain is already a link, with nothing to create first. | Created in the dashboard or API, or long links with /a/key_live_… on a custom domain. Routing by path needs $deeplink_path and custom logic. | DeepLinkNow | [6] [7] |
| Advertising IDs | The SDKs never read them, so there's no ATT prompt | Collected by default (FULL protection level: advertising IDs and device IDs) | DeepLinkNow | [8] |
| Ad-blocker lists | Not on any of them | Branch domains and its web SDK are on AdGuard and EasyPrivacy, and EasyPrivacy blocks about 4,195 Branch customer link domains. | DeepLinkNow | [9] [10] |
| Typical contract | Published on the site: $0, $49, $149 or $499 a month, paid monthly or yearly, and Enterprise from $500 a month | Median about $55K a year (Vendr, 61 deals) | DeepLinkNow | [11] |

## Where DeepLinkNow is ahead

- A free plan for up to 25,000 monthly active users, deferred deep links included, and you don't need a card to start.
- Your own domain from $49 a month on Startup, set up in the dashboard.
- No DeepLinkNow domain is on AdGuard or EasyPrivacy, so ad blockers don't stop the link page.
- iOS clipboard handoff on every plan: the link page copies the link and the SDK reads it on first launch.
- Any path on your link domain is already a link, with no prefix and nothing to create first.
- There's no attribution, and the SDKs never read advertising IDs or need the ATT prompt. A deferred link can be claimed for 1 hour after the click, and stored fingerprints are deleted within 30 days.
- Free AASA, assetlinks.json and ad-block checkers you can use without signing up.

## Pick Branch if…

- You need attribution, ad network integrations and campaign analytics, and someone else's budget pays for it.
- You want Journeys web banners and a marketing team running links without developers.

If you just need links that open the right screen after install, don't pay for the rest.

## The pricing math

Branch's Intro plan is $39 a month with 5,000 volume credits, 500 links or QR codes and 25,000 clicks. Past that it bills $0.01 a click, $0.05 a link and $0.05 a volume credit, with no cap. I bill on monthly active users instead. [1] [3]

Say your links get 40,000 clicks a month. On Intro that's $39 plus 15,000 extra clicks at $0.01, so $189 before any volume-credit overage, and still no custom domain. On DeepLinkNow it's free while the app stays under 25,000 monthly users and 1,000 distinct paths, or $49 on Startup with your own domain. A custom domain on Branch means Activation Basics, $199 a month.

## Switching from Branch

1. Add the DLN SDK next to the one you have and ship it.
2. Point your link domain at DLN. Paths on it work straight away.
3. Read the link with checkDeferredDeepLink() on first launch.
4. Remove the Branch SDK in the next release.

## Questions

### How does Branch's pricing compare with DeepLinkNow's?

Branch's Intro plan is $39 a month with 5,000 volume credits, 500 links or QR codes and 25,000 clicks. Past that it bills $0.01 a click, $0.05 a link and $0.05 a volume credit, with no cap. I bill on monthly active users instead. Say your links get 40,000 clicks a month. On Intro that's $39 plus 15,000 extra clicks at $0.01, so $189 before any volume-credit overage, and still no custom domain. On DeepLinkNow it's free while the app stays under 25,000 monthly users and 1,000 distinct paths, or $49 on Startup with your own domain. A custom domain on Branch means Activation Basics, $199 a month.

### When is Branch the better choice?

You need attribution, ad network integrations and campaign analytics, and someone else's budget pays for it. You want Journeys web banners and a marketing team running links without developers.

### Can I run DeepLinkNow next to Branch?

Yes. The SDK doesn't depend on any other deep linking SDK, so you can ship both, move your link domain over, and remove the old one later.

# DeepLinkNow vs AppsFlyer

Mobile measurement platform (MMP). As of October 2026, with a public source for every claim.

AppsFlyer is the biggest attribution platform there is, and if you spend serious money on paid installs it's very good at its job. Deep linking is one feature inside that, and it's no longer on the free plan, so deferred links mean a sales call and an attribution contract.

| | DeepLinkNow | AppsFlyer | Stronger | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Free plan | Free for up to 25,000 monthly active users, deferred deep links included, and you don't need a card to start | Zero plan: links and QR codes, but no deferred deep linking since its 2026 update | DeepLinkNow | [1] [2] |
| Sales call | Only for Enterprise (from $500/mo). Developer, Startup, Growth and Scale are self-serve. | Every paid tier is "Request a demo" | DeepLinkNow | [1] |
| Plan with a custom domain | $49/mo (Startup) | Only through sales. Branded domains start on the Advanced tier and deferred deep links on Deep Linking Standard, both at custom prices. | DeepLinkNow | [1] |
| Making links | Any path on your domain is already a link, with nothing to create first. | Short links are created through the OneLink API (each gets an ID of up to 50 characters) or the dashboard. API links don't show up in the dashboard list. | DeepLinkNow | [5] |
| Ad-blocker lists | Not on any of them | 54 rules on AdGuard Tracking Protection, including onelink.me and the OneLink Smart Script | DeepLinkNow | [3] |
| Advertising IDs | The SDKs never read them, so there's no ATT prompt | With ATT support on, the iOS SDK collects the IDFA on iOS 14.5 and later | DeepLinkNow | [6] |
| Typical contract | Published on the site: $0, $49, $149 or $499 a month, paid monthly or yearly, and Enterprise from $500 a month | Median about $88.5K a year (Vendr, 130 deals) | DeepLinkNow | [4] |

## Where DeepLinkNow is ahead

- A free plan for up to 25,000 monthly active users, deferred deep links included, and you don't need a card to start.
- Published prices: $0, $49, $149 or $499 a month. You only talk to me if you want Enterprise.
- Your own domain from $49 a month on Startup, set up in the dashboard.
- No DeepLinkNow domain is on AdGuard or EasyPrivacy, so ad blockers don't stop the link page.
- Any path on your link domain is already a link, with no prefix and nothing to create first.
- There's no attribution, and the SDKs never read advertising IDs or need the ATT prompt. A deferred link can be claimed for 1 hour after the click, and stored fingerprints are deleted within 30 days.
- iOS clipboard handoff on every plan: the link page copies the link and the SDK reads it on first launch.

## Pick AppsFlyer if…

- You spend real money on paid user acquisition and need attribution, fraud protection and SKAdNetwork reporting.

If you just need links that open the right screen after install, don't pay for the rest.

## The pricing math

AppsFlyer bills on conversions: its last published rate was $0.07 for every install or action its links drove, after a first-year welcome package of 12,000. Deferred deep links now sit in the Deep Linking Suite at a custom price on top, and buyers on Vendr report a median contract of about $88.5K a year. [7] [1] [4]

Say your links bring in 10,000 installs a month. At $0.07 a conversion that's $700 a month to AppsFlyer before the Deep Linking Suite, which is extra and priced by sales. On DeepLinkNow the same app is $49 a month on Startup for up to 100,000 monthly users with your own domain, and installs aren't charged at all.

## Switching from AppsFlyer

1. Add the DLN SDK next to the one you have and ship it.
2. Point your link domain at DLN. Paths on it work straight away.
3. Read the link with checkDeferredDeepLink() on first launch.
4. Keep AppsFlyer for attribution if you still need it. The DLN SDK runs next to it.

## Questions

### How does AppsFlyer's pricing compare with DeepLinkNow's?

AppsFlyer bills on conversions: its last published rate was $0.07 for every install or action its links drove, after a first-year welcome package of 12,000. Deferred deep links now sit in the Deep Linking Suite at a custom price on top, and buyers on Vendr report a median contract of about $88.5K a year. Say your links bring in 10,000 installs a month. At $0.07 a conversion that's $700 a month to AppsFlyer before the Deep Linking Suite, which is extra and priced by sales. On DeepLinkNow the same app is $49 a month on Startup for up to 100,000 monthly users with your own domain, and installs aren't charged at all.

### When is AppsFlyer the better choice?

You spend real money on paid user acquisition and need attribution, fraud protection and SKAdNetwork reporting.

### Can I run DeepLinkNow next to AppsFlyer?

Yes. The SDK doesn't depend on any other deep linking SDK, so you can ship both, move your link domain over, and remove the old one later.

# DeepLinkNow vs Adjust

Mobile measurement platform (MMP). As of October 2026, with a public source for every claim.

Adjust is built for teams buying ads, and deep linking (TrueLink) lives inside its attribution product. You create links in Campaign Lab, the SDK collects advertising IDs, and Adjust's own docs say deferred links may be limited for anyone who opts out of tracking. If all you want is the right screen after an install, that's a lot of machinery, plus a sales contract, to get it.

| | DeepLinkNow | Adjust | Stronger | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Deferred deep linking | On every plan, including the free one | In TrueLink Base. The deep link generator API and the faster ODDL path need TrueLink Core or Enterprise. | DeepLinkNow | [1] [9] |
| Published prices | Published on the site: $0, $49, $149 or $499 a month, paid monthly or yearly, and Enterprise from $500 a month | Through sales only. Buyers on Vendr report a median of $44,000 a year (31 deals), ranging from $10,800 to $370,080. | DeepLinkNow | [8] |
| After an ATT opt-out | Nothing changes, because no advertising IDs are involved. | "Deferred deep linking may be limited for users that opt-out." | DeepLinkNow | [2] |
| iOS clipboard handoff | On every plan, including the free one | LinkMe: iOS 15 and up, SDK 4.31.0, and only if the user is in Safari | DeepLinkNow | [3] |
| Making links | Any path on your domain is already a link, with nothing to create first. | Created in Campaign Lab or through the API, as short links on yourbrand.go.link/<token> | DeepLinkNow | [4] [5] |
| Plan with a custom domain | $49/mo (Startup) | Not offered: you get a branded name in front of .go.link, which can't be changed after you save it. | DeepLinkNow | [5] |
| Advertising IDs | The SDKs never read them, so there's no ATT prompt | The Android SDK adds the AD_ID permission by default. The iOS SDK's privacy manifest declares tracking, with eight tracking domains. | DeepLinkNow | [6] [7] |
| Ad-blocker lists | Not on any of them | adj.st, the legacy link domain, is on AdGuard Tracking Protection, and app.adjust.com is on EasyPrivacy | DeepLinkNow | [10] [11] |

## Where DeepLinkNow is ahead

- Published prices: $0, $49, $149 or $499 a month. You only talk to me if you want Enterprise.
- There's no attribution, and the SDKs never read advertising IDs or need the ATT prompt. A deferred link can be claimed for 1 hour after the click, and stored fingerprints are deleted within 30 days.
- iOS clipboard handoff on every plan: the link page copies the link and the SDK reads it on first launch.
- Any path on your link domain is already a link, with no prefix and nothing to create first.
- No DeepLinkNow domain is on AdGuard or EasyPrivacy, so ad blockers don't stop the link page.
- Your own domain from $49 a month on Startup, set up in the dashboard.
- Hosted in Sydney (Vercel syd1, database in AWS ap-southeast-2), if that matters to your users or your lawyers.

## Pick Adjust if…

- You buy ads and need attribution, including SKAdNetwork when users opt out of tracking.
- You ship games or less common platforms: Adjust has SDKs for Unity, Cocos2d-x, Steamworks, Windows and more.

Sources: [2] [12]

If you just need links that open the right screen after install, don't pay for the rest.

## The pricing math

Adjust bills on attributions and sells its paid plans through sales. Buyers on Vendr report a median contract of $44,000 a year. [8]

Vendr's median Adjust contract is $44,000 a year, about $3,670 a month, and the smallest it lists is $10,800 a year, about $900 a month. My Growth plan is $149 a month for up to 500,000 monthly active users. If what you need from Adjust is links that open the right screen, that's all you'd pay.

## Switching from Adjust

1. Add the DLN SDK next to the one you have and ship it.
2. Point your link domain at DLN. Paths on it work straight away.
3. Read the link with checkDeferredDeepLink() on first launch.
4. Keep Adjust for attribution if you still need it. The DLN SDK runs next to it.

## Questions

Adjust bills on attributions and sells its paid plans through sales. Buyers on Vendr report a median contract of $44,000 a year. Vendr's median Adjust contract is $44,000 a year, about $3,670 a month, and the smallest it lists is $10,800 a year, about $900 a month. My Growth plan is $149 a month for up to 500,000 monthly active users. If what you need from Adjust is links that open the right screen, that's all you'd pay.

You buy ads and need attribution, including SKAdNetwork when users opt out of tracking. You ship games or less common platforms: Adjust has SDKs for Unity, Cocos2d-x, Steamworks, Windows and more.

Yes. The SDK doesn't depend on any other deep linking SDK, so you can ship both, move your link domain over, and remove the old one later.

# DeepLinkNow vs Singular

Mobile measurement platform (MMP). As of October 2026, with a public source for every claim.

Singular is a solid attribution platform, and to its credit the free plan includes deferred deep links. The catch is that every Singular deep link is also an attribution link: you make it on their link page and it carries their tracking. If you don't run ads, you'd be adopting an MMP just to get links.

| | DeepLinkNow | Singular | Stronger | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Free plan | Free for up to 25,000 monthly active users, deferred deep links included, and you don't need a card to start | Free: 15,000 paid conversions, deferred deep linking included, no card | Level | [1] [7] |
| Paid plans | Published on the site: $0, $49, $149 or $499 a month, paid monthly or yearly, and Enterprise from $500 a month | Growth at $0.05 per conversion through "Let's Talk", and Enterprise by demo | DeepLinkNow | [1] |
| Plan with a custom domain | $49/mo (Startup) | Only through sales, on Growth ($0.05 per conversion, through "Let's Talk") or Enterprise | DeepLinkNow | [1] [4] |
| Making links | Any path on your domain is already a link, with nothing to create first. | Created on the Create Link page as sng.link/<app id>/<link id>, with the target in _dl and _ddl. Every deep link is an attribution link. | DeepLinkNow | [2] [3] |
| iOS clipboard handoff | The link page copies the link before the App Store opens and the SDK reads it on first launch, with a scored match as the backup | Needs your own landing page with Singular's Web SDK and a download button | DeepLinkNow | [5] |
| Deferred click window | 1 hour: long enough for an install and first launch, short enough that an old click can't go to the wrong person | 6 hours by default, 24 on request through your Customer Success Manager | Level | [3] |
| Advertising IDs | The SDKs never read them, so there's no ATT prompt | The iOS SDK's privacy manifest declares tracking, and it collects the IDFA when the user allows it | DeepLinkNow | [6] |
| Ad-blocker lists | Not on any of them | singular.net on EasyPrivacy; its SDK and web SDK hosts on AdGuard Tracking Protection | DeepLinkNow | [8] [9] |

## Where DeepLinkNow is ahead

- Any path on your link domain is already a link, with no prefix and nothing to create first.
- There's no attribution, and the SDKs never read advertising IDs or need the ATT prompt. A deferred link can be claimed for 1 hour after the click, and stored fingerprints are deleted within 30 days.
- Your own domain from $49 a month on Startup, set up in the dashboard.
- iOS clipboard handoff on every plan: the link page copies the link and the SDK reads it on first launch.
- No DeepLinkNow domain is on AdGuard or EasyPrivacy, so ad blockers don't stop the link page.
- Every fingerprint match comes back with a 0 to 100 score and a HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW label, so you decide what to trust.
- Hosted in Sydney (Vercel syd1, database in AWS ap-southeast-2), if that matters to your users or your lawyers.

## Pick Singular if…

- You run paid user acquisition and want attribution, cost aggregation (Singular lists 1,200+ connectors), SKAdNetwork and fraud prevention.

Sources: [1] [10]

If you just need links that open the right screen after install, don't pay for the rest.

## The pricing math

Singular bills on paid conversions: 15,000 free, then $0.05 each on Growth. I bill on monthly active users and don't count conversions at all. [1]

A custom domain on Singular means Growth, which starts with a sales conversation. If you run ads and get 30,000 paid conversions a month, that's up to $1,500 a month on Growth at $0.05 each. An app with 100,000 monthly users is $49 a month on my Startup plan, however many conversions it gets.

## Switching from Singular

1. Add the DLN SDK next to the one you have and ship it.
2. Point your link domain at DLN. Paths on it work straight away.
3. Read the link with checkDeferredDeepLink() on first launch.
4. Keep Singular for attribution if you still need it. The DLN SDK runs next to it.

## Questions

### How does Singular's pricing compare with DeepLinkNow's?

Singular bills on paid conversions: 15,000 free, then $0.05 each on Growth. I bill on monthly active users and don't count conversions at all. A custom domain on Singular means Growth, which starts with a sales conversation. If you run ads and get 30,000 paid conversions a month, that's up to $1,500 a month on Growth at $0.05 each. An app with 100,000 monthly users is $49 a month on my Startup plan, however many conversions it gets.

### When is Singular the better choice?

You run paid user acquisition and want attribution, cost aggregation (Singular lists 1,200+ connectors), SKAdNetwork and fraud prevention.

### Can I run DeepLinkNow next to Singular?

Yes. The SDK doesn't depend on any other deep linking SDK, so you can ship both, move your link domain over, and remove the old one later.

# DeepLinkNow vs Kochava

Mobile measurement platform (MMP). As of October 2026, with a public source for every claim.

Kochava's free plan includes deferred deep links, which is generous for an attribution platform. What it leaves out is Universal Links, App Links and your own domain. Those start on Foundation at $500 a month, and the domain gets set up by your Client Success Manager.

| | DeepLinkNow | Kochava | Stronger | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Free plan | Free for up to 25,000 monthly active users, deferred deep links included, and you don't need a card to start | Free App Analytics: 10,000 attributed conversions a month, with deferred deep linking and SmartLinks, but no Universal Links, App Links or custom domain | DeepLinkNow | [1] [2] |
| Paid plans | Published on the site: $0, $49, $149 or $499 a month, paid monthly or yearly, and Enterprise from $500 a month | Foundation from $500/mo (33,000 conversions) and Enterprise from $2,000/mo, both starting with a trial request form | DeepLinkNow | [1] |
| Plan with a custom domain | $49/mo (Startup) | From $500/mo (Foundation): a your-brand.smart.link subdomain, set up through your Client Success Manager | DeepLinkNow | [1] [6] |
| Making links | Any path on your domain is already a link, with nothing to create first. | Create a SmartLink first, then pass the destination in a parameter you configure, such as ?deeplink= | DeepLinkNow | [3] |
| Deferred matching | The link page copies the link before the App Store opens and the SDK reads it on first launch, with a scored match as the backup | IP address and user agent by default. Kochava's test guide tells testers to turn off iCloud Private Relay. | DeepLinkNow | [4] |
| Match lookback | 1 hour: long enough for an install and first launch, short enough that an old click can't go to the wrong person | 7 days for modeled (IP and user agent) matches, by default | Level | [5] |
| Advertising IDs | The SDKs never read them, so there's no ATT prompt | IDFA after the ATT prompt (the SDK can show it) and the Google advertising ID, through optional modules | DeepLinkNow | [7] |
| Ad-blocker lists | Not on any of them | kochava.com/track/ on EasyPrivacy, smart.link/imp/ on AdGuard Tracking Protection | DeepLinkNow | [8] [9] |

## Where DeepLinkNow is ahead

- Your own domain from $49 a month on Startup, set up in the dashboard.
- There's no attribution, and the SDKs never read advertising IDs or need the ATT prompt. A deferred link can be claimed for 1 hour after the click, and stored fingerprints are deleted within 30 days.
- Any path on your link domain is already a link, with no prefix and nothing to create first.
- iOS clipboard handoff on every plan: the link page copies the link and the SDK reads it on first launch.
- Every fingerprint match comes back with a 0 to 100 score and a HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW label, so you decide what to trust.
- No DeepLinkNow domain is on AdGuard or EasyPrivacy, so ad blockers don't stop the link page.
- Hosted in Sydney (Vercel syd1, database in AWS ap-southeast-2), if that matters to your users or your lawyers.

## Pick Kochava if…

- You run paid campaigns and want attribution and fraud prevention.
- You ship to TVs and consoles as well as phones: Kochava has SDKs and SmartLinks for connected TV.

Sources: [1]

If you just need links that open the right screen after install, don't pay for the rest.

## The pricing math

Kochava bills on attributed conversions: installs or re-engagements credited to a media source. 10,000 a month are free, Foundation includes 33,000 from $500 a month. [1] [2]

An app with 50,000 monthly users that wants Universal Links, App Links and its own link domain: on Kochava that's Foundation, from $500 a month, with the domain set up through your Client Success Manager. On DeepLinkNow the same app is $49 on Startup, own domain included, and Universal Links and App Links work on every plan, free one too.

## Switching from Kochava

1. Add the DLN SDK next to the one you have and ship it.
2. Point your link domain at DLN. Paths on it work straight away.
3. Read the link with checkDeferredDeepLink() on first launch.
4. Keep Kochava for attribution if you still need it. The DLN SDK runs next to it.

## Questions

### How does Kochava's pricing compare with DeepLinkNow's?

Kochava bills on attributed conversions: installs or re-engagements credited to a media source. 10,000 a month are free, Foundation includes 33,000 from $500 a month. An app with 50,000 monthly users that wants Universal Links, App Links and its own link domain: on Kochava that's Foundation, from $500 a month, with the domain set up through your Client Success Manager. On DeepLinkNow the same app is $49 on Startup, own domain included, and Universal Links and App Links work on every plan, free one too.

You run paid campaigns and want attribution and fraud prevention. You ship to TVs and consoles as well as phones: Kochava has SDKs and SmartLinks for connected TV.

Yes. The SDK doesn't depend on any other deep linking SDK, so you can ship both, move your link domain over, and remove the old one later.

5. [Kochava: attribution overview](https://support.kochava.com/articles/reference-information/223-attribution-overview/)
6. [Kochava: Universal Link and App Link support](https://support.kochava.com/articles/links-overview/16919-adding-universal-link-or-app-link-support/)
7. [Kochava Apple SDK](https://support.kochava.com/articles/apple-sdk/)
8. [EasyPrivacy filter list](https://easylist.to/easylist/easyprivacy.txt)
9. [AdGuard Tracking Protection filter](https://filters.adtidy.org/extension/ublock/filters/3.txt)

# DeepLinkNow vs Airbridge

Mobile measurement platform (MMP). As of October 2026, with a public source for every claim.

Airbridge is a full measurement platform with deep linking built in, and it's priced fairly for one. It still works like an MMP though: you create links up front, the SDK reads advertising IDs, and on iOS your app can be left waiting on the tracking prompt before it gets the deferred link.

| | DeepLinkNow | Airbridge | Stronger | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Free plan | Free for up to 25,000 monthly active users, deferred deep links included, and you don't need a card to start | There isn't one. Core starts at $40/mo after a 30-day trial. | DeepLinkNow | [1] [2] |
| What you pay for | Monthly active users, one flat price per plan | Data points: 500K a month on Core, then $0.0001 each | Level | [2] |
| Making links | Any path on your domain is already a link, with nothing to create first. | Created first, in the dashboard, Google Sheets or the API. Custom domains must be a dedicated subdomain. | DeepLinkNow | [3] |
| Deferred link on iOS | Handed over on first launch, with no prompt to wait for. | The SDK waits for the ATT answer (30 seconds by default) before delivering it | DeepLinkNow | [4] |
| Advertising IDs | The SDKs never read them, so there's no ATT prompt | IDFA and GAID collected by default | DeepLinkNow | [5] |
| Ad-blocker lists | Not on any of them | SDK, attribution and event domains, plus a deferred-deeplink rule, on AdGuard's tracking list | DeepLinkNow | [6] |

## Where DeepLinkNow is ahead

- A free plan for up to 25,000 monthly active users, deferred deep links included, and you don't need a card to start.
- There's no attribution, and the SDKs never read advertising IDs or need the ATT prompt. A deferred link can be claimed for 1 hour after the click, and stored fingerprints are deleted within 30 days.
- Any path on your link domain is already a link, with no prefix and nothing to create first.
- No DeepLinkNow domain is on AdGuard or EasyPrivacy, so ad blockers don't stop the link page.
- iOS clipboard handoff on every plan: the link page copies the link and the SDK reads it on first launch.
- Every fingerprint match comes back with a 0 to 100 score and a HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW label, so you decide what to trust.

## Pick Airbridge if…

- You want a full MMP, with ad network integrations and attribution.

If you just need links that open the right screen after install, don't pay for the rest.

## The pricing math

Airbridge's Core plan starts at $40 a month for 500,000 data points, then $0.0001 per data point. Its pricing calculator counts about 14.4 data points per monthly user at its default setting: 8,000 users is 115,200 data points and 50,000 users is 720,000. [1] [2]

At 100,000 monthly users, Airbridge's calculator works out to about 1.44 million data points: $40 plus 940,000 extra at $0.0001, so about $134 a month, and more as you track more events. On DeepLinkNow, Startup is a flat $49 a month for up to 100,000 monthly users with your own domain, and below 25,000 monthly users it's free.

## Switching from Airbridge

1. Add the DLN SDK next to the one you have and ship it.
2. Point your link domain at DLN. Paths on it work straight away.
3. Read the link with checkDeferredDeepLink() on first launch.
4. Remove the Airbridge SDK, and its ATT prompt if deep linking was its only job.

## Questions

### How does Airbridge's pricing compare with DeepLinkNow's?

Airbridge's Core plan starts at $40 a month for 500,000 data points, then $0.0001 per data point. Its pricing calculator counts about 14.4 data points per monthly user at its default setting: 8,000 users is 115,200 data points and 50,000 users is 720,000. At 100,000 monthly users, Airbridge's calculator works out to about 1.44 million data points: $40 plus 940,000 extra at $0.0001, so about $134 a month, and more as you track more events. On DeepLinkNow, Startup is a flat $49 a month for up to 100,000 monthly users with your own domain, and below 25,000 monthly users it's free.

### When is Airbridge the better choice?

You want a full MMP, with ad network integrations and attribution.

### Can I run DeepLinkNow next to Airbridge?

Yes. The SDK doesn't depend on any other deep linking SDK, so you can ship both, move your link domain over, and remove the old one later.

## Sources

1. [Airbridge pricing](https://www.airbridge.io/en/pricing)
2. [Airbridge Core plan](https://airbridge.io/en/plans/core)
3. [Airbridge: tracking links](https://help.airbridge.io/en/deeplink-guides/understanding-tracking-link.md)
4. [Airbridge React Native SDK](https://help.airbridge.io/en/deeplink-developers/react-native-sdk-v4.md)
5. [Airbridge: identifiers](https://help.airbridge.io/en/guides/identifiers.md)
6. [AdGuard Tracking Protection filter](https://filters.adtidy.org/extension/ublock/filters/3.txt)

# DeepLinkNow vs Detour

Deferred deep linking for React Native and Expo. As of October 2026, with a public source for every claim.

Detour is the closest thing to what I built: deferred deep links for React Native and Expo, without an attribution suite. What I like about it: the Expo Router support is solid, it has a nice pattern for holding a link until the user gets past your sign-in screen, and it's made by Software Mansion, who know React Native as well as anyone. Where we differ is the free plan, what your own domain costs, URLs without an app hash in them, and how much your app gets told about each match.

| | DeepLinkNow | Detour | Stronger | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Free plan | Free for up to 25,000 monthly active users, deferred deep links included, and you don't need a card to start | 1,500 clicks a month and 50 short links per app. Past the limit, deep link matching stops and plain redirects keep working. | DeepLinkNow | [1] |
| What you pay for | Monthly active users (devices that open your app with the SDK). Each distinct link path counts once toward the link limit (1,000 on the free plan). | Link clicks: Starter $19/mo for 70,000, Scale $79/mo for 350,000, then optional pay-as-you-go per 1,000 clicks | Level | [1] |
| Plan with a custom domain | $49/mo (Startup) | $79/mo (Scale). Free and Starter links live on a .godetour.link subdomain. | DeepLinkNow | [1] [4] |
| Making links | Any path on your domain is already a link, with nothing to create first. | Any path and query after the app's fixed /<app_hash>/ segment, which stays in the URL on a custom domain too | DeepLinkNow | [2] [4] |
| What the app gets | A confidence score from 0 to 100 with a HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW label, and you pick the threshold | A link, or nothing. You set one threshold in the dashboard (850 by default, 700 to 1200), and the app never sees the score, so it can't treat a near miss differently. | DeepLinkNow | [3] [4] |
| Match window | 1 hour: long enough for an install and first launch, short enough that an old click can't go to the wrong person | 15 minutes by default, configurable from 5 to 180 | Level | [3] |
| Expo Router | A +native-intent helper (@deeplinknow/react-native/expo-router) and a useDeferredDeepLink() hook | A +native-intent handler and a DetourProvider, with examples that keep the link through sign-in | Level | [4] [6] |
| How long click data is kept | A deferred link can be claimed for 1 hour after the click, and stored fingerprints are deleted within 30 days. | The privacy policy says data is kept "as long as needed to provide" the service and gives no period | DeepLinkNow | [7] |
| Smart banner | A tracker-free script for your website on Startup and up, with no impression counting, cookies or extra requests | A script on Starter and up, with templates, scheduling and impression counts | Level | [4] |
| Instagram and TikTok | On iOS the link page gets out of Instagram, Threads and Facebook to the App Store, and walks TikTok users through opening it in their browser | Hands off out of Instagram, Threads and Facebook on iOS, with a browser prompt for TikTok | Level | [4] |
| Scheduled exports | Signed daily, weekly or monthly link counts to your HTTPS endpoint on paid plans, plus a CSV download | Signed daily, weekly or monthly analytics to your HTTPS endpoint on paid plans | Level | [4] |

## Where DeepLinkNow is ahead

- A free plan for up to 25,000 monthly active users, deferred deep links included, and you don't need a card to start.
- Your own domain from $49 a month on Startup, set up in the dashboard.
- Every fingerprint match comes back with a 0 to 100 score and a HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW label, so you decide what to trust.
- Any path on your link domain is already a link, with no prefix and nothing to create first.
- Free AASA, assetlinks.json and ad-block checkers you can use without signing up.
- Hosted in Sydney (Vercel syd1, database in AWS ap-southeast-2), if that matters to your users or your lawyers.

## Pick Detour if…

- You'd rather depend on Software Mansion, a well-known React Native company with a big open-source track record.

Sources: [5]

If you want a free plan sized for a real launch and a score you can set your own threshold on, try mine first.

## The pricing math

Detour bills on link clicks: 1,500 free, 70,000 for $19, 350,000 for $79. I bill on monthly active users, the devices that open your app with the SDK. The two don't convert one to one, so it depends on how many clicks each user makes. [1]

Say 15,000 people use your app each month and your links get 40,000 clicks across a few hundred paths. Detour: Starter, $19. DeepLinkNow: free. Now put the links on your own domain: Detour needs Scale, $79 a month, and the /<app_hash>/ segment stays in every URL. On DeepLinkNow it's $49 on Startup for up to 100,000 monthly users, however many clicks they make.

## Switching from Detour

1. Add the DLN SDK next to Detour's and ship it.
2. Point your link domain at DLN. Paths on it work without the /<app_hash>/ segment.
3. Swap createDetourNativeIntentHandler for createRedirectSystemPath from @deeplinknow/react-native/expo-router, and DetourProvider's link for useDeferredDeepLink().
4. Keep Detour until the links you've already shared stop getting clicks. Its custom-domain links stop resolving when the subscription ends.

## Questions

### How does Detour's pricing compare with DeepLinkNow's?

Detour bills on link clicks: 1,500 free, 70,000 for $19, 350,000 for $79. I bill on monthly active users, the devices that open your app with the SDK. The two don't convert one to one, so it depends on how many clicks each user makes. Say 15,000 people use your app each month and your links get 40,000 clicks across a few hundred paths. Detour: Starter, $19. DeepLinkNow: free. Now put the links on your own domain: Detour needs Scale, $79 a month, and the /<app_hash>/ segment stays in every URL. On DeepLinkNow it's $49 on Startup for up to 100,000 monthly users, however many clicks they make.

### When is Detour the better choice?

You'd rather depend on Software Mansion, a well-known React Native company with a big open-source track record.

### Can I run DeepLinkNow next to Detour?

Yes. The SDK doesn't depend on any other deep linking SDK, so you can ship both, move your link domain over, and remove the old one later.

## Sources

1. [Detour: billing](https://detour.swmansion.com/docs/platform/fundamentals/billing)
2. [Detour: click handling](https://detour.swmansion.com/docs/platform/architecture/click-handling)
3. [Detour: matching](https://detour.swmansion.com/docs/platform/architecture/matching)
4. [Detour docs (full text)](https://detour.swmansion.com/docs/llms-full.txt)
